info.title: ONLYOFFICE DocSpace API
info.description: REST API of ONLYOFFICE DocSpace - a multi-tenant platform for document management, collaboration and file sharing. Requests are authenticated with the portal session cookie, an API key, Basic credentials, or an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect token; see the security schemes of this document.

servers.description: The production DocSpace portal, at the customer's own domain.

get.description:
Returns all portal applications of the installation, each with its state on the current portal. An application
is a feature module that the portal can turn on and configure, such as `ai-rooms` or `docs-cloud`. The
installation configuration sets the list and the default state of each application. The API cannot add or
remove applications. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The list follows the order of the
configuration, without paging or a total. The `settings` field is empty until the portal saves settings for
the application. An empty list means that the installation has no applications, not that all are turned off. To
read one application, use `GET api/2.0/apps/{id}`. To change the state or the settings, use
`PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/enabled` or `PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`.

200.description: The portal applications configured on this installation, each with the enabled state and the settings of the current portal

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns one portal application with its state on the current portal. An application is a feature module that
the portal can turn on and configure, such as `ai-rooms` or `docs-cloud`. Take the identifier from
`GET api/2.0/apps`. It is case-sensitive. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The `settings`
field is empty until the portal saves settings for the application. To read only the settings, use
`GET api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`. If the installation has no application with this identifier, the call
returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The application to read, by the identifier `GET api/2.0/apps` reports - one of the feature modules the portal
can turn on, such as `ai-room` or `docs-cloud`. An identifier not declared in the installation configuration
answers 404, which is also how a caller learns that an application does not exist here.

200.description: The application with the enabled state and the settings of the current portal

404.description: No application with this identifier is configured on this installation

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns only the settings of one portal application on the current portal. The answer is the saved JSON value
itself, not an application object. Take the identifier from `GET api/2.0/apps`. It is case-sensitive. Any
signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The portal returns the value as it was saved and never
checks its shape. An empty result means that the portal has never saved settings for the application. Then
the application uses its own defaults. To read the enabled state, use `GET api/2.0/apps/{id}`. If the
installation has no application with this identifier, the call returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The application to read, by the identifier `GET api/2.0/apps` reports - one of the feature modules the portal
can turn on, such as `ai-room` or `docs-cloud`. An identifier not declared in the installation configuration
answers 404, which is also how a caller learns that an application does not exist here.

200.description: The settings document saved for the application, or an empty result if the portal has never saved one

404.description: No application with this identifier is configured on this installation

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Saves the settings of one portal application for the current portal. Take the identifier from
`GET api/2.0/apps`. It is case-sensitive. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and
DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. It
replaces the whole saved value and does not merge into it. So first read the current value with
`GET api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`, change it, and send it complete. The portal accepts any JSON value and never
checks its shape. If `settings` is `null` or missing, the call deletes the saved value. Then the application
uses its own defaults. The call returns the application in its new state, with the saved settings. It does not
change the enabled state. To turn the application on or off, use `PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/enabled`. The call
returns 400 if the body is not valid JSON. If the installation has no application with this identifier, the
call returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The application whose configuration is stored, by the identifier `GET api/2.0/apps` reports. An identifier
not declared in the installation configuration answers 404.

requestBody.description: The configuration to store for this portal, replacing whatever was stored before.

schema.description: The configuration to store for this portal, replacing whatever was stored before.

200.description: The application in its new state, with the stored settings document

400.description: The request body is not a valid JSON document, so no settings are stored

403.description: The caller has no portal-settings right

404.description: No application with this identifier is configured on this installation

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Turns one portal application on or off for the current portal. Take the identifier from `GET api/2.0/apps`. It
is case-sensitive. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. The call changes data. It saves the flag for this portal instead of the default from the
configuration. You can repeat it with the same body. Turning an application off keeps its saved settings. They
apply again when you turn it on. The call returns the application in its new state, with its settings. To
change the settings, use `PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`. The call returns 400 if the body is not valid JSON or
has no `enabled` field. If the installation has no application with this identifier, the call returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The application to switch, by the identifier `GET api/2.0/apps` reports. It has to be an application declared
in the installation configuration; an unknown identifier answers 404 rather than creating anything.

requestBody.description:
The new state of the application. Only the enabled flag travels here; the settings document is changed
through `PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`.

schema.description:
The new state of the application. Only the enabled flag travels here; the settings document is changed
through `PUT api/2.0/apps/{id}/settings`.

200.description: The application in its new state, with the saved settings document left untouched

400.description: The request body is not a valid JSON document or has no enabled field, so the state is not changed

403.description: The caller has no portal-settings right

404.description: No application with this identifier is configured on this installation

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns whether the request carries a valid sign-in to the current portal. The call checks the authentication
cookie or the token in the `Authorization` header. Anyone can call it without signing in. It is read-only and
also works while the portal is unpaid. It returns `true` for a signed-in user and `false` in every other case.
A `false` result gives no reason. The token may be missing, malformed, expired, or revoked. To sign in again,
use `POST api/2.0/authentication`. To learn who the caller is, use `GET api/2.0/people/@self`.

200.description: `true` when the request carries a valid token or cookie of an active portal user, `false` in every other case

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Signs a user in to the current portal and returns an authentication token. If the user has a second factor, the
call returns what that factor needs instead. Send `userName` with `password` or `passwordHash`, a confirmation
link in `confirmData`, or a third-party account. Anyone can call it without signing in. The call changes data.
Each successful call opens a new session. You can repeat it with the same password or third-party account. After
a sign-in with a `confirmData` link, a repeated call with this link returns 404. A new `culture` also becomes
the user's language. With SMS codes on, the answer has `sms` and no `token`. Without an activated phone number,
`confirmUrl` holds a phone activation link for `POST api/2.0/authentication/setphone`. Otherwise the call sends
an SMS code. It sends none while an earlier code is still valid. With an authenticator app on, the answer has
`tfa` and no `token`. Before the app is connected, the answer also has its setup key in `tfaKey`. To finish such
a sign-in, send the code to `POST api/2.0/authentication/{code}`. The call returns 401 for a wrong password, an
unknown user, or a rejected third-party account. It also returns 401 if the portal does not allow third-party
sign-in. A rejected `confirmData` key or its unknown user returns 404. The call returns 403 for a disabled user,
a wrong CAPTCHA, or too many failed attempts. Failed attempts count per user name and IP address. During a
block, a solved CAPTCHA in `recaptchaResponse` lets the call through. The portal's login settings set the
attempt limit and the block time. If `confirmData.email` is not an email address, the call returns 400.

schema.description: The credentials a sign-in is attempted with: a portal password, a confirmation key, or a third-party account.

200.description: The authentication token, or the second factor that has to be passed before a token is issued

400.description: The request body could not be validated, for example `confirmData.email` is not an email address

401.description: The password, the confirmation key or the third-party profile was rejected, or third-party sign-in is not allowed for this portal

403.description: The user is disabled, or too many failed attempts and CAPTCHA failures have blocked further sign-ins for these credentials

404.description: No user of this portal matches the credentials in the request body

429.description: The portal rate limiter rejected the call - retry after the interval in the `Retry-After` header

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Finishes a two-factor sign-in with a one-time code and returns the authentication token. Call it after `POST
api/2.0/authentication` returns `sms` or `tfa`. Send the same credentials again, with the code in `code`. With
SMS codes on, the call checks an SMS code. Otherwise it checks an authenticator app code or a backup code.
Anyone can call it without signing in. The call changes data. An SMS code or a backup code works only once, so a
repeated call returns 401. An app code is accepted again for up to 5 minutes, and each call opens a new session.
An accepted SMS code cancels the other codes and activates the phone number. The first accepted app code
connects the app and creates backup codes. A new `culture` also becomes the user's language. The answer has
`token`, and `sms` or `tfa` shows the checked factor. To get a new SMS code, use `POST
api/2.0/authentication/sendsms`. The call returns 401 for a wrong, empty, or expired code. It also returns 401
if the user has no second factor. After too many wrong SMS codes, even a right one returns 401 for up to 10
minutes. More app code attempts than the portal's login attempt limit return 401 until one minute passes without
attempts. A wrong password or an unknown user also returns 401. The call returns 403 for a disabled user or too
many failed password attempts. A rejected key in `confirmData` returns 404. If `confirmData.email` is not an
email address, the call returns 400.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The two-factor authentication code. Send the same value as the `code` of the request body, which is the one the handler reads.

schema.description: The same credentials as an ordinary sign-in, plus the one-time code that completes it.

200.description: The authentication token to send in the `Authorization` header, together with the second factor that was accepted

400.description: The request body could not be validated, for example `confirmData.email` is not an email address

401.description: The credentials were rejected, or the two-factor code is wrong, empty or expired

403.description: The user is disabled, or too many failed attempts have blocked further sign-ins for these credentials

404.description: No user of this portal matches the credentials in the request body

429.description: The portal rate limiter rejected the call - retry after the interval in the `Retry-After` header

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Ends the session of the authentication cookie that comes with the request. The token of that session stops
working, and the call clears the portal cookies. A token sent only in the `Authorization` header stays valid.
To end such a session, use `PUT api/2.0/security/activeconnections/logout/{loginEventId}`. Anyone can call it
without signing in. Without a session cookie, the call ends nothing. You can repeat it. Other sessions of the
user stay open. To end them, use `PUT api/2.0/security/activeconnections/logoutallexceptthis`. For a user who
signed in through SSO, the call can return a single logout URL. It does so when SSO is on and has an SLO
address. Open this URL to end the session at the identity provider too. For other users, the result is empty.

200.description: The single logout URL to open when the user signed in through SSO, or an empty result when no further action is needed

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Checks the key of a confirmation link and returns whether the link can still be used. Links include
invitations, phone activation, password changes, and portal deletion. Take `key`, `type`, and the other values
from the query string of the link. If `key` is empty, the call uses the confirmation cookie of this `type`.
Anyone can call it without signing in, even on an unpaid, suspended, or blocked portal. For a signed-out
caller, the call is read-only. It does not accept an invitation or sign anyone in. A signed-in caller with a
room's shared invitation link joins that room with the link's role. The call also counts one use of that link.
A repeated call changes nothing. For a signed-in caller, a valid invitation link returns `UserExisted` instead
of `Ok`. Follow only an `Ok` result with the action of the link. For an invitation, use `POST api/2.0/people`
with `fromInviteLink`. For a sign-in link, use `POST api/2.0/authentication` with `confirmData`. If the
portal's IP restrictions block the caller, an invitation link returns 403. The call returns 400 if `email` is
not a valid email address.

schema.description: The confirmation link parameters to check.

200.description: Whether the confirmation link may be used, with the room and the email it was issued for when it is an invitation

400.description: The request body cannot be read, or `email` is sent but empty or not a valid email address

403.description: The portal's IP restrictions do not allow this address to check an invitation link

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Saves the phone number of a user and sends an SMS code to it. Use it when `POST api/2.0/authentication`
returns `sms` with a phone activation link in `confirmUrl`. Sign the request with the confirmation token from
that link. An anonymous call or an invalid or expired link returns 401. An authentication token alone returns
403. The call changes data. It saves the number as not activated. The number becomes activated when
`POST api/2.0/authentication/{code}` accepts a code sent to it. If a code sent to this number is still valid,
the call sends no new SMS. You can repeat it to change a number that is not activated yet. The answer has no
token. To send another code, use `POST api/2.0/authentication/sendsms`. The call cannot change an activated
number. If SMS codes are on for the user but the portal cannot send them, the call returns 405. It still saves
the number but sends no SMS.

schema.description: The phone number a user going through phone activation registers for SMS codes.

200.description: The masked phone number the code was sent to and the moment that code expires - no authentication token yet

401.description: The request carries no confirmation token from a phone activation link, or the link is invalid or expired

403.description: The request is signed with an authentication token instead of the phone activation link

405.description: SMS two-factor is switched on for the user but the portal cannot send SMS codes, for example because its plan does not include them; the number is stored and no code is sent

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Sends a new SMS code to the stored phone number of a user. Use it to resend the code after
`POST api/2.0/authentication` returns `sms`. The call checks the credentials in the body as
`POST api/2.0/authentication` does. Anyone can call it without signing in. Each call sends another SMS and counts
toward the SMS usage of the portal. Earlier codes stay valid until they expire, by default after 10 minutes. The
first accepted code cancels every code of the number. By default, a number gets at most 6 codes until its newest
code expires. You can repeat the call up to this limit. After it, wait until the newest code expires. The answer
has no token. To finish the sign-in, send the code to `POST api/2.0/authentication/{code}`. The call returns 401
for a wrong password or an unknown user. It returns 403 for a disabled user or after too many failed attempts. A
rejected key in `confirmData` returns 404. If the user has no stored phone number, the call returns 400. If SMS
codes are off on the portal or for the user, it returns 405.

schema.description: The credentials a sign-in is attempted with: a portal password, a confirmation key, or a third-party account.

200.description: The masked phone number the code was sent to and the moment that code expires - no authentication token yet

400.description: The request body could not be validated, for example `confirmData.email` is not an email address

401.description: The password, the confirmation key or the third-party profile was rejected

403.description: The user is disabled, or too many failed attempts have blocked further sign-ins for these credentials

404.description: No user of this portal matches the credentials in the request body

405.description: SMS two-factor is not available on the portal or not required for this user, so there is no code to send

429.description: The portal rate limiter rejected the call - retry after the interval in the `Retry-After` header

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the portal sign-in methods: LDAP, external identity providers, SAML single sign-on, and the built-in
identity server. A login app calls it before the user signs in. Anyone can call it without signing
in. It also works while the portal is not paid. The call is read-only. Only the `providers` list depends on
the caller. Its order follows the country of the caller's IP address. On a server installation, mobile apps
do not get Facebook and Apple ID in it. If the portal cannot read the settings of a method, it reports the
method as off. The call still succeeds. The answer holds no settings of these methods. To read them, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2` and `GET api/2.0/settings/authservice`. Both need the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.

200.description: The sign-in methods the portal offers: LDAP, the external identity providers, single sign-on and the identity server, each with the state it has for this portal

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the names of the source products this installation can import a portal from. Pass a name as
`migratorName` to `POST api/2.0/migration/init/{migratorName}`, which ignores case. Requires a DocSpace admin.
Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The names are not localized, for example `GoogleWorkspace` or
`Nextcloud`. The list keeps the order in which the installation registers its migrators. It depends on the
installation, not on the portal. The parse call does not reject a name outside this list. Instead, its job
ends with an error in `GET api/2.0/migration/status`.

200.description: The names of the migrators this installation can import from, in registration order

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Starts a job that reads the uploaded backup of the portal with the migrator named in the path. The job lists
the users, the groups, and the archives it cannot open. Users without an email and users that already exist
come in lists of their own. First, call `migrationFileUpload.ashx` with `Init=true`. This opens a new upload
folder and deletes the previous one. Then post each part of the archive to it with `Name` set to the file
name. Take `migratorName` from `GET api/2.0/migration/list`. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The call only queues the job and returns an empty body immediately. Repeat `GET api/2.0/migration/status`
until `isCompleted` is true. Then read the result from `parseResult` and any failure from `error`. The job
changes nothing on the portal. To import, edit `parseResult` and send it to `POST api/2.0/migration/migrate`.
A portal runs one job at a time. While a parse or an import runs, the call does nothing and reports nothing.
After the job ends, a repeated call starts a new parse. A failed parse deletes the backup, so upload it again
first. If the backup is larger than the storage quota of the portal, the job ends with an error.

parameters.name: migratorName
parameters.description:
The migrator that knows the format of the uploaded backup. It has to be one of the names
`GET api/2.0/migration/list` reports for this installation, spelled exactly as listed.

200.description: The parse job has been queued; the response carries no content and the result is read from `GET api/2.0/migration/status`

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the progress and the result of the parse or import job of the portal. The other operations of this
group only queue work, so their outcome appears here. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until `isCompleted` is true. A failed job also sets
`isCompleted` to true, so then check `error`. If the portal has no job, the call returns 200 with an empty
result. This happens before the first parse and after `POST api/2.0/migration/finish`. To read each step of
the job, use `GET api/2.0/migration/logs`.

200.description: The state of the parse or import queued for the portal, or an empty result when the portal has no job

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Stops the parse job of the portal and deletes the uploaded backup. Use it after a wrong archive or a wrong
migrator name. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call only queues the request and returns
an empty body. Soon after, `GET api/2.0/migration/status` no longer shows the parse. You cannot restore the
deleted backup. Before a new parse, upload it to `migrationFileUpload.ashx` again. You can repeat the call. With
no parse job, it still returns 200 and deletes the upload folder. The call does not stop an import. It still
deletes the backup that the import reads. To delete a finished import, use `POST api/2.0/migration/clear`.

200.description: The cancellation has been queued; the parse stops and the uploaded backup is deleted. The response carries no content

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Deletes the finished import job of the portal and the backup uploaded for it. Call it after
`GET api/2.0/migration/status` reports `isCompleted` for a job whose `parseResult.operation` is `migration`.
Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The users, groups, and files already imported stay on the
portal. The call only queues the request and returns an empty body. You can repeat it. With nothing to clear,
it still returns 200. After it runs, `GET api/2.0/migration/status` returns an empty result. Also,
`GET api/2.0/migration/logs` returns 404, so download the log first. The call does not stop a running parse or
import. It still deletes the backup they read. To stop a parse, use `POST api/2.0/migration/cancel`. You do
not need this call after `POST api/2.0/migration/finish`, which does the same clean-up.

200.description: The clean-up has been queued; the finished import is dropped and the uploaded data deleted. The response carries no content

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Starts the import of the users, groups, and files selected in the body from the parsed backup. First, call
`POST api/2.0/migration/init/{migratorName}` and wait until `isCompleted` is true. Then send `parseResult`
from `GET api/2.0/migration/status` back here. Mark the users and groups to import with `shouldImport`, and
the content with the `import` flags. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. Only the portal owner
can import a user as `DocSpaceAdmin` who is not a DocSpace admin of this portal yet. If another admin tries
this, the call returns 403 and imports nothing. The call only queues the job and returns an empty body
immediately. Repeat `GET api/2.0/migration/status` until `isCompleted` is true. There, `successedUsers`,
`failedUsers`, and `error` show the result. The log in `GET api/2.0/migration/logs` has a line for each step.
The import changes the portal and cannot be undone. Do not repeat the call. While the job runs, a repeated
call does nothing. After the job ends, the portal deletes the backup. A repeated call then starts a job that
fails and replaces the result and the log of the import. So read them first, and upload and parse the backup
before a new import. The call returns 400 for a missing or unreadable body, an unknown `userType`, or an empty
or invalid `email`. When the import ends, close it with `POST api/2.0/migration/finish`. That call can also
email the imported users their activation links.

Raises the `room.created` webhook for every room the queued import creates. Raises the `folder.created` webhook for every folder the queued import creates, including one per imported user for their files. Raises the `room.updated` webhook for every room the queued import moves to its owner, a room admin or DocSpace admin.

schema.description: The migration API information.

200.description: The import has been queued; the response carries no content and the progress is read from `GET api/2.0/migration/status`

400.description: The request body is missing or could not be read as a parse result, including an unknown `userType` name, or a user in `users`, `withoutEmailUsers` or `existUsers` has an `email` that is empty or not a valid address

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator, or is not the portal owner and asked to import a user as `DocSpaceAdmin` who is not an administrator of this portal yet

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: for every folder the queued import creates, including one per imported user for their files
for every room the queued import creates
for every room the queued import moves to its owner, a room admin or DocSpace admin

get.description:
Returns the log of the parse or import job of the portal as a file. The log has a timestamped line for each
step, including why the job skipped a user or file. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only. The body is not JSON. It is `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, sent as the attachment
`migration.log`. Each job has its own log, and the call returns the log of the job that
`GET api/2.0/migration/status` shows. The portal saves the log only when the job ends. So wait until
`isCompleted` is true, since the call fails while the job runs. If the portal has no job, the call
returns 404. This happens after `POST api/2.0/migration/clear` or `POST api/2.0/migration/finish`.

post.description:
Closes a finished import and can email the imported users their activation links. Call it after
`GET api/2.0/migration/status` reports `isCompleted` for the import. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers
get 403. If `isSendWelcomeEmail` is true, the call emails each imported user who is not active yet. With
`false`, it sends nothing, and you can invite these users later. Then it queues the same clean-up as
`POST api/2.0/migration/clear`. The clean-up deletes the job and the uploaded backup, and the imported data
stays. The call returns an empty body. After it, `GET api/2.0/migration/status` returns an empty result. Also,
`GET api/2.0/migration/logs` returns 404, so download the log first. You can repeat the call with `false`.
With `true`, do not repeat it. A repeat can send the emails again. It returns 400 if the body has no
`isSendWelcomeEmail`.

post.description:
Sends one event from an integration module to the open DocSpace pages of the request host's portal. Set
exactly one addressee, `user` or `room`. With `user`, only that portal user's open sessions receive it. With
`room`, everyone in the portal subscribed to `plugin-{module}-{room}` receives it. Browsers receive the
socket event `plugin:{module}:{event}` with `{ message }`. The key, not the body, sets `{module}`. Anyone
can call it without signing in, with the module key in the `X-Module-Key` header. A missing or unknown key
returns 401. The installation administrator issues each key for a list of portals. A key not allowed for
this portal returns 403. The call only queues the event for delivery and stores nothing. A user with no open
session never sees the event. Each repeated call delivers the event again. If the portal's payment has
lapsed, the call returns 402. If `user` names no active user of this portal, the call returns 404. The call
returns 400 for a missing body, an invalid event or room name, or not exactly one addressee. A body over
64 KB returns 413.

The secret key the installation administrator issued to the module. It is not a user or portal credential:
the module the event belongs to is the one this key is configured for, so the key is the module's identity.

put.description:
Starts the purchase of a monthly paid plan for the portal and returns the URL of the hosted checkout page.
Nothing is bought until the buyer completes that page. The plan becomes active after the payment provider
confirms the payment. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. It also returns 403 if the
installation has no billing service. The call itself is read-only, so you can repeat it. If the portal already
has a paid plan, the call returns an empty result. If the billing service fails, the call also returns an empty
result. Repeated calls then return it for up to 10 minutes. To change a paid plan, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/update`. The URL carries the email of the caller and the language of the request.
It also carries a currency that the call picks from the IP address of the caller. The page redirects to
`successUrl` or `backUrl` when the buyer finishes or cancels. Take a monthly plan for `quantity` from
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas`. The call returns 400 if `quantity` holds more than one product or a
quantity of zero or less. It also returns 400 for a yearly plan or a wallet service. To buy wallet services,
use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`. The call returns 402 if the portal already exceeds a limit of
the requested plan. These limits cover admins, users, rooms, AI agents, and storage.

put.description:
Changes the number of admins that the paid plan of the portal covers. The payment provider bills the
difference to the payment method on file. The portal needs a plan bought with
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/url`. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404. The payer is
the portal user whose email is the email of the billing customer. Only the payer can call it. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call spends money. If the
provider accepted the change, a repeated call with the same quantity returns 400. The call returns `true` if
the provider accepted the change. It returns `false` if the provider declined it, or if the call failed or
timed out. After a failure the change may still be applied, so check the plan before you repeat the call. On
a priced plan, `quantity` must name the current plan from `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quota`. The call
returns 400 for more than one product, another plan, or a wallet service. It returns 402 if the portal
already exceeds a limit of the plan in the new quantity. By default, the limit is 10 calls a minute per user.
More calls return 429. To buy wallet services, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`.

put.description:
Buys units of a wallet service, or schedules the quantity of the service for the next period. The mode comes
from `productQuantityType`. With `Add`, the call buys the units immediately and pays for them from the portal
wallet. With `Set`, the call charges nothing and changes the quantity from the next period. With `Set`, an
empty quantity cancels a change that was scheduled earlier. With a zero quantity, the portal does not renew the
service at the next period. The call returns 400 for `Renew` and `Sub`. If the portal has no billing customer,
the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the
installation has no billing service. An `Add` call spends money. Do not repeat an `Add` call. Each call buys
the units again. You can repeat a `Set` call with the same body. With `Add`, the wallet needs a sub-account in
the accounting currency with enough money. If the wallet has no such sub-account, the call returns 404. If the
billing service declines the purchase, fails, or cannot be reached, the call returns 402. The call returns 402
for an add-on to the plan if the plan payment is overdue. A trial plan passes this check. The call returns 400
if the quantity is below the minimum of the service. By default, the minimum is 100 units for disk storage and
10 for Docs Connect Dev Pack. With `Add`, the minimum for admins is the number
of admins the portal already has. With `Add`, the call checks the minimum only while the portal does not have
the service yet. With `Add`, an empty or zero quantity also returns 400. While Docs Connect is active, a
request for Docs Connect Dev Pack returns 400. To move to Docs Connect Dev Pack, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/switchtodevpack`. While Docs Connect Dev Pack is active, `Set` with Docs
Connect schedules the return to it. The return happens at the next period and needs a quantity above zero. In
this case, `Add` with Docs Connect returns 400. With `Add`, the call returns `true`. With `Set`, it returns
`true`, or `false` if the portal does not have the service or cannot save the change. By default, the limit
is 10 calls a minute per user. More calls return 429. To get the price first, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/calculatewallet`.

Returns the price of a wallet service purchase without making it. Use it to show the amount before the user
confirms the purchase. The call returns 400 if `productQuantityType` is not `Add` or the quantity is not above
zero. It also returns 400 if the product is not a wallet service. If the portal has no billing customer or no
wallet sub-account in the accounting currency, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call is read-only and buys
nothing, so you can repeat it. To make the purchase, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`. The price
is for the moment of the call and is not reserved. So it can change before the purchase. If the billing
service fails, the call returns 200 with an empty body.

Returns the unused part of the current paid subscription period of the portal, in money. This is the credit
that `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/subscription/movetowallet` moves to the wallet. If the portal has no billing
customer, the call returns 404. The payer is the portal user whose email is the email of the billing customer.
Only the payer can call it. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no
billing service. The call is read-only. If the plan is not paid, the call returns 402. It also returns 402 if
the billing service fails or cannot be reached. If the paid plan has no subscription, the call returns 404. If
the paid plan is a wallet product or has no product ID, the call returns 400. The figures are for the moment
of the call, so they change between calls.

post.summary: Move the subscription to the wallet
post.description:
Ends the paid subscription of the portal and moves the portal to the wallet. First, the call adds the unused
balance of the period to the wallet. Then it tops up the wallet from the payment method if that credit does
not cover the price. Then it buys the requested number of admins as a wallet service. To read the credit
first, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/subscription/balance`. If the portal has no billing customer, the call
returns 404. If the customer has no payment method, the call returns 403. The payer is the portal user whose
email is the email of the billing customer. Only the payer can call it. Other callers get 403. The call also
returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call spends money and cannot be undone. Do not
repeat it. The call ends the subscription before it buys the admins. If the purchase fails, the call returns
`false` with 200. The portal is then on the wallet, with the credit and any top-up in it. To buy the admins
after that, use `Add` in `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`. With a delayed payment method, the call
does not top up the wallet. Then the wallet must already cover the price. The call returns `true` if the
admins were bought. The product in `quantity` must be the admins wallet service. The call returns 400 for
another product or a quantity of zero or less. It also returns 400 for fewer admins than the portal already
has. If the paid plan is a wallet product, the call returns 400. If the plan is not paid, the call returns
402. It also returns 402 if the balance cannot be moved. The next two errors come after the subscription has
ended. If the wallet still lacks money after the top-up, the call returns 402. If the wallet has no
sub-account in the accounting currency, the call returns 404. If the paid plan has no subscription, the call
returns 404. By default, the limit is 10 calls a minute per user. More calls return 429.

200.description: `true` when the balance was moved to the wallet and the administrators were bought; `false` when the subscription has ended and the balance was moved, but the purchase of the administrators failed

Returns the address of the portal page where the payer manages the billing account. The page shows the payment
method, the invoices, and the receipts. The address is relative to the portal root. The call adds `backUrl` to
the address as a query parameter. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns an empty result to
any caller. The payer is the portal user whose email is the email of the billing customer. Otherwise, only the
payer or the portal owner can call it. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation
has no billing service. The call is read-only. If `backUrl` is not a valid URL or is too long, the call
returns 400. The page buys nothing. To buy a plan, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/url`. To attach a payment
method, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/checkoutsetupurl`.

`quantity` takes in the purchase operations. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal
owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. All prices are in one currency,
which the call picks from the IP address of the caller. If no product has a price in that currency, the call
uses EUR in Europe and USD elsewhere. A product without a price in the chosen currency has the price 0. So 0
means that the product has no price, not that it is free. To read the currencies of the portal, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/currencies`. To read the current plan with its limits and usage, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quota`.

get.summary: Get the current plan and limits
get.description:
Returns the quota of the portal, paid or free, with the limits of its features and their usage. Any signed-in
user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. The call is read-only. By default, the call reads the plan
from the cache. With `refresh=true`, it reads the plan from the billing service, so use it right after a
purchase. The answer depends on the user type of the caller. A DocSpace admin or the portal owner gets the
price, the due date, and all features. A room admin gets only the `manager`, `room`, `total_size`, and
`statistic` features. A user gets only the `total_size` feature. For a room admin and a user, `price` is an
empty object and `dueDate` is missing. If the plan has the `statistic` feature or the installation is
standalone, every caller gets `usersQuota`, `roomsQuota`, `aiAgentsQuota`, and `tenantCustomQuota`. To read the
quotas that the portal can buy, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas`.

start-up needs and costs nothing; asking for a fresh one makes a remote call, so use it right after a
purchase or a top-up and not on every read.

of the billing customer. If the portal has a billing customer with an email, only the payer can call it. Other

caller. The page redirects to `successUrl` or `backUrl` when the user finishes or cancels. If `backUrl` or

the payer. The payer is the portal user whose email is the billing email. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other
callers get 403. The call is read-only. The call returns an empty result if the installation has no billing
service. It also returns an empty result if the portal has no billing customer. If no portal user has the
billing email, `payer` is empty. Then nobody can call the operations that only the payer can call. By default,
the call reads the customer from the cache. With `refresh=true`, it reads the customer from the billing
provider. Use it right after a payment method is attached.

post.description:
Charges the payment method of the portal and adds the amount to the portal wallet. The wallet services are
paid from this balance. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404. If the customer has no
payment method, the call returns 403. To attach one, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/checkoutsetupurl`. The
payer is the portal user whose email is the email of the billing customer. Only the payer can call it. Other
callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call spends money.
Do not repeat it. Each call charges the payment method again. If the call returns `false` or times out, check
the balance before you repeat it. With a delayed payment method, the balance shows the money only after the
transfer settles. The call returns 400 if `currency` is not a supported accounting currency or `amount` is out
of range. The call returns `true` if the payment provider accepted the charge. To read the new balance, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/balance`. By default, the limit is 10 calls a minute per user. More calls
return 429.

amount for each currency and the last credit movement. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The

`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/deposit` adds to it. To list the movements, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operations`. Each call reads the balance from the accounting service, so
it is current right after a top-up too. Only a failed read is cached. A read fails if the service cannot be
reached or does not know the portal. Then the call returns an empty result for 10 minutes. Use `refresh=true`
to read it again immediately.

get.description:
Returns a page of the money movements of the portal wallet. The movements are top-ups, service charges,
refunds, and corrections. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the
installation has no billing service. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns an empty result.
The call is read-only. All filters are optional. If `serviceName` has a name that the installation does not
sell, the call returns 404. If neither `credit` nor `debit` is set, the list has both directions. AI usage
paid with the portal's own provider keys has the service names `ai-tools-byok` and `ai-search-byok`. The
`serviceName` filter accepts them. Such a movement looks like its AI service, with `byok` set. By default,
`offset` is 0 and `limit` is 25. The answer repeats them next to `totalQuantity`, `totalPage`, and
`currentPage`. To get the same data as a file, use `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operationsreport`. To
get the totals per service, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
The number of movements to skip before the first one returned, for walking through a long history page by
page. Counted after the filters and the ordering are applied, and starts at 0 when omitted.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
The maximum number of movements returned in one page. Defaults to 25 when omitted; the answer echoes the
window back next to `totalQuantity`, `totalPage` and `currentPage`, so the next `offset` can be computed
without counting the items.

parameters.name: serviceName
parameters.description:
The wallet services whose movements are kept, named the way the billing catalogue names them - `backup`,
`ai-tools`, `ai-search`, `disk-storage`, `docscloud`. Take the values from the `serviceName` field of
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/walletservices`; the match ignores case, a name this installation does not sell
fails the call with 404, and an omitted list keeps every service. A bare string is accepted in place of an
array for backward compatibility.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description:
The beginning of the reported period, inclusive. Read in the portal time zone rather than in UTC, so a
movement at the edge of the period falls where the portal sees it; defaults to the portal creation date.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description:
The end of the reported period, inclusive. Read in the portal time zone rather than in UTC, and defaults to
the moment the call is made.

parameters.name: participantName
parameters.description:
The participant whose movements are kept - the account the accounting service records as the cause of a
movement. A movement caused by a portal user carries that user ID here, and one caused by the portal itself
carries the customer name; surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and an omitted value keeps every participant.

parameters.name: credit
parameters.description:
Whether movements that add money to the wallet - top-ups, refunds and corrections in the portal's favour -
are kept. Both directions are reported when neither this nor `debit` is given.

parameters.name: debit
parameters.description:
Whether movements that take money out of the wallet - the charges of the wallet services - are kept. Both
directions are reported when neither this nor `credit` is given.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The kind of movement to keep, which says what caused the money to move rather than how it ended. Every kind
is reported when it is omitted.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
The outcome to keep. A movement that is still being settled is reported as pending and may change later,
while the other outcomes are final; every outcome is reported when this is omitted.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
The name of the field the movements are sorted by, spelled as the accounting service names it, such as
`StartDate` or `ServiceName`. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and the accounting service applies its own
ordering when this is omitted.

parameters.name: orderType
parameters.description:
The direction the field named in `orderBy` is sorted in. Newest or largest first is what the accounting
service does by default, so leaving this out sorts the same way as asking for descending explicitly.

Returns the consumption and the cost of each wallet service of the portal, added up per service. Requires a
DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service.
If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns an empty result. The call is read-only. All filters
are optional. If `serviceName` has a name that the installation does not sell, the call returns 404. The
amounts use the unit of each service. For AI tools, the unit is tokens, not AI credits. AI usage paid with the
portal's own provider keys has totals of its own, `ai-tools-byok` and `ai-search-byok`. They have the title of
their AI service and `byok` set, and `serviceName` accepts these names. With `mergeByok=true`, the call adds
them to the totals of their AI services. To list the charges behind the totals, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operations`. To get the same figures as a file, use
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/report`.

parameters.description:
The wallet services whose consumption is added up, named the way the billing catalogue names them -
`backup`, `ai-tools`, `ai-search`, `disk-storage`, `docscloud`. Take the values from the `serviceName` field
of `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/walletservices`; the match ignores case, a name this installation does not
sell fails the call with 404, and an omitted list covers every service.

The participant whose consumption is added up - the account the accounting service records as the consumer.
Consumption caused by a portal user carries that user ID here; surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and an

while the other outcomes are final; every outcome is counted when this is omitted.

defaults to the portal creation date.

the moment the call is made.

must all match for a record to be counted. The keys are chosen by the service that writes them, so read them
off the `metadata` of the records already returned rather than guessing; an omitted map counts every record.

ordering are applied, and starts at 0 when omitted.

the window back with its paging information, so the next `offset` can be computed without counting the items.

services that an admin turned on by hand. It also has the Docs Connect trial, which the wallet does not pay
for. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no

post.description:
Starts a job that builds the history of the wallet movements as an `xlsx` file. If the portal has no billing
customer, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if
the installation has no billing service. The call queues the job and returns it. The file is not ready when
the response arrives. The body takes the filters of `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operations`. An empty
body covers the time from the creation of the portal until now. If `serviceName` has a name that the
installation does not sell, the call returns 404. The file marks the AI services paid with the portal's own
provider keys, `ai-tools-byok` and `ai-search-byok`, as BYOK. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operationsreport` until `isCompleted` is true. Then take the file from
`resultFileUrl` or `resultFileId`. The portal saves the file in the My documents section of the caller. The
file counts against the portal storage. Each user has one report of this kind at a time. While it runs, a
repeated call returns the running job. After `isCompleted` becomes true, a repeated call starts a new job that
builds a new file. To stop a running job, use `DELETE api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/operationsreport`. If the
build fails, the job ends with `error` filled in.

usage or monthly usage reports. An empty result means that the caller has no operations report. Either none
was started, or the job was stopped or removed. Starting a new report removes the completed job. So read the

wrong filters or a report that is no longer needed. If the portal has no billing customer, the call
returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no
billing service. The call queues a stop request for the worker that builds the file. So

repeat the call. If the caller has no running report, the call does nothing. The response has no body. A 200
response means that the stop was requested, not that a report was stopped. The call does not stop the service
usage or monthly usage reports. A finished report keeps its file in My documents.

delete.description:
Stops the `xlsx` service usage report that the caller has running and removes its job. Use it for a report
with wrong filters or a report that is no longer needed. If the portal has no billing customer, the call
returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation
has no billing service. The call queues a stop request for the worker that builds the file. So
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/report` can still return the job for a short time. You can repeat
the call. If the caller has no running report, the call does nothing. The response has no body. A 200 response
means that the stop was requested, not that a report was stopped. The call does not stop the operations or
monthly usage reports. A finished report keeps its file in My documents.

post.description:
Starts a job that builds the wallet spending per calendar month as an `xlsx` file. If the portal has no
billing customer, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also
returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call queues the job and returns it. The file is
not ready when the response arrives. The body takes only the period, `startDate` and `endDate`. An empty body
covers the time from the creation of the portal until now. The call cuts the months in the portal time zone,
as `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/monthly` does. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/monthly/report` until `isCompleted` is true. Then take the file
from `resultFileUrl` or `resultFileId`. The portal saves the file in the My documents section of the caller.
The file counts against the portal storage. Each user has one report of this kind at a time. While it runs, a
repeated call returns the running job. After `isCompleted` becomes true, a repeated call starts a new job that
builds a new file. To stop a running job, use `DELETE api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/monthly/report`.
If the build fails, the job ends with `error` filled in. The body has no service filter. For a report per
service, use `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/report`.

Returns the state of the `xlsx` monthly usage report that the caller started with
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage/monthly/report`. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until
`isCompleted` is true. While the build runs, `percentage` shows its progress. When the file is ready,
`resultFileId`, `resultFileName`, and `resultFileUrl` point to it. The file is in the My documents section of
the caller. If the build fails, `error` is filled in. If the portal has no billing customer, the call
returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no
billing service. The call is read-only. It returns only the monthly usage report of the caller, not the
operations or service usage reports. An empty result means that the caller has no monthly usage report. Either
none was started, or the job was stopped or removed. Starting a new report removes the completed job. So read
the file link from the first answer with `isCompleted` true.

get.summary: Get the service prices from the accounting service
get.description:
Returns the price list of one wallet service as the accounting service keeps it. Requires a DocSpace admin.
Other callers get 403. It also returns 403 if the installation has no billing or accounting service. The call
is read-only. By default, the list also has retired prices and prices that have not started yet. With
`active=true`, the list has only the prices in force now. A service without prices returns an empty list. The
amounts are in the currency of the service, which the records do not name. The installation caches the list
for all portals for up to an hour. So a change in the accounting service can take an hour to appear. To read
the current prices that the customer sees, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas`. If `serviceName` is too
long, the call returns 400.

parameters.name: serviceName
parameters.description:
The service whose price list is read, named the way the billing catalogue names it, such as `ai-tools` or
`backup`. Take the value from the `serviceName` field of `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/walletservices`.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description:
Whether the answer is narrowed to the prices in force at the moment of the call. Leaving it false also
returns the retired and the not yet started ones, which is what pricing a movement recorded in the past
needs.

200.description: The list of the service prices

400.description: The `serviceName` is longer than 255 characters

get.description:
Returns one spending limit on the AI services of the portal by its ID. A limit applies to the portal as a
whole, to every user, or to one user. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns
403 if the installation has no billing service. The call is read-only. The answer has the scope, thresholds,
period, and state of the limit, but no spending. To read the spending of the portal, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit/total`. To read the spending of each user, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit/participants`. The call returns 404 if the portal has no billing
customer or no AI service limit with this ID. If `id` is zero or negative, the call returns 400.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the service limit, as returned in `id` by the operation that created it or by the reads of limits.

delete.description:
Deletes one spending limit on the AI services. This can be the limit of the portal, the limit for every user,
or a personal limit. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin.
Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call cannot
be undone. To keep the settings of a limit, turn it off with `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`
instead. To get a deleted limit back, create a new one with `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`. After
a personal limit is deleted, the limit for every user applies to that user. The call returns 404 if the portal
has no AI service limit with this ID. A repeated call returns 404. The response has no body. If `id` is zero
or negative, the call returns 400.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the service limit, as returned in `id` by the operation that created it or by the reads of limits.

400.description: The ID is zero or negative

get.description:
Returns the spending limit on the AI services for the portal as a whole. The spending of all users counts
towards this limit. The answer also has the spending in the current period and what is left. The spending
includes the expected cost of AI operations that still run. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call is read-only. The AI services
check this limit together with the limits of the users. So a user can reach it before their own limit. If the
limit is not set or was deleted, the call returns 200 with a null `response`. To create it, use
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit` with the scope `Total`. A turned-off limit is returned with
`enabled` false. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404.

200.description: The limit of the portal as a whole with its spending, or null when no such limit is set

get.description:
Returns the spending limit on the AI services for every user. It applies to each user separately, if the user
has no personal limit in force. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if
the installation has no billing service. The call is read-only. The answer has no spending, since each user
has their own. To read the spending of each user, use `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit/participants`.
The `periodEnd` field still shows when the current period ends for everyone. If the limit is not set or was
deleted, the call returns 200 with a null `response`. To create it, use
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit` with the scope `Global`. A turned-off limit is returned with
`enabled` false. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404.

get.description:
Returns a page of the spending limits on the AI services that apply to the portal users. Each item has what
the user spent in the current period and what is left. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The
call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. If the portal has no billing customer, the
call returns 404. The call is read-only. If the portal has no limits, the page is empty. A personal limit wins
over the limit for every user. An item with the scope `Custom` is a personal limit. An item with the scope
`Global` is the limit for every user. Its ID repeats for each user that it applies to. The list has no
turned-off limits. A user who has not used the AI services yet can be missing. By default, `offset` is 0 and
`limit` is 25. The answer repeats them next to `totalQuantity`, `totalPage`, and `currentPage`. By default,
the newest limits come first. The call returns 400 if `offset`, `limit`, `orderBy`, or `orderType` is out of
range.

parameters.description: The number of limits to skip before the first one returned, counted in the sort order of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The largest number of limits one page holds.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: The field the list is sorted by: the user a limit applies to, or the moment it was created.

parameters.name: orderType
parameters.description: The direction the field named in `orderBy` is sorted in.

200.description: A page of the limits in force for the users with their spending and paging information

400.description: `offset` is negative, `limit` is outside the allowed page size, or `orderBy` or `orderType` is not one of its values

put.description:
Sets the same personal spending limit on the AI services for each listed portal user. It replaces the personal
limit that a user already has and turns it on. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404.
Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing
service. The call returns 400 if neither `amountValue` nor `quantityValue` is set. If a user in `userIds` does
not exist, the call returns 404. The call changes data. A user listed twice gets one limit. The call returns
400 for an empty list or more than 1000 users. So split a larger group into several calls. Unlike
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`, this call sets the whole limit. So a threshold that you leave out
is removed. The period can change. A lifetime limit that stays lifetime keeps its count. Each personal limit
applies instead of the limit for every user. The AI services also check the limit of the portal. You can
repeat the call with the same body. The accounting service can reject a threshold with 400. The call returns
the number of personal limits that it set. To list them, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit/participants`.

post.description:
Creates a spending limit on the AI services, which are AI tools and AI search together. The `scope` field sets
whom the limit applies to. The scope `Total` is for the portal as a whole, and `Global` is for every user
separately. The scope `Custom` is for the user in `userId`. Only `Custom` takes `userId`, and other cases
return 400. A personal limit applies to its user instead of the limit for every user. The AI services also
check the limit of the portal. If the portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404. Requires a
DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service.
The call changes data. The call returns 400 if neither `amountValue` nor `quantityValue` is set. With both,
the AI services stop when either is reached. The accounting service can also reject a threshold with 400. An
example is a quantity for services with different units. If the user does not exist, the call returns 404. A
second limit of the same scope or for the same user returns 409. So a repeated call returns 409. To change a
limit, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`. You cannot change the scope, the user, or the period
later.

put.description:
Changes the thresholds of a spending limit on the AI services, or turns it off and on with `enabled`. If the
portal has no billing customer, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The
call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The call changes data, but only in the
fields that you send. An omitted threshold keeps its value, so you cannot remove a threshold here. To remove
one, delete the limit with `DELETE api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit/{id}`. Then create it again with
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`. This is also the way to change the scope, the user, or the period.
A turned-off limit stops restricting the AI services immediately. A new threshold applies from the next AI
operation. If it is below the spending, the AI services stop until the period ends. You can repeat the call
with the same body. The call returns 404 if the portal has no AI service limit with this ID. The accounting
service can reject a threshold with 400. An example is a quantity for services with different units.

put.description:
Turns off every personal spending limit on the AI services. Each user then falls back to the limit for every
user, if it is set. The limit of the portal and the limit for every user do not change. If the portal has no
billing customer, the call returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also
returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The turned-off limits stop restricting their users
immediately. The portal keeps them, so you can turn each one back on with
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit`. The call changes data, and a repeated call turns off nothing more.
The call returns the number of limits that it turned off, or 0 if none was in force. To turn off the limit of
one user, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit` with `enabled` set to false.

get.description:
Returns the automatic top-up settings of the portal wallet. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The portal does not need a billing customer or a billing service. The call is read-only. If the portal never
set up the top-up, the call returns the defaults. Then `enabled` is false, `currency` is null, and
`minBalance` and `upToBalance` are 0. These zeros are out of range for
`POST api/2.0/portal/payment/topupsettings`. So send real values instead of the defaults. Until the portal
first saves the settings, `lastModified` is `0001-01-01T00:00:00`. The portal sets `lowBalanceThreshold` and
`lowBalanceNotified`, and you cannot change them.

200.description: The automatic top-up settings of the portal, or their defaults when it has never configured them

post.description:
Turns the automatic top-up of the portal wallet on or off and sets its thresholds. While it is on, the portal
charges the payment method when the balance falls below `minBalance`. The charge brings the balance up to
`upToBalance` in `currency`. If the portal has no billing customer or no wallet balance, the call returns 404.
To create the balance, top up the wallet once with `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/deposit`. The payer is the
portal user whose email is the email of the billing customer. Only the payer can call it. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service. The body replaces all stored
settings, and an omitted body resets them to the defaults. The call returns 400 if `minBalance` or
`upToBalance` is missing or out of range. It also returns 400 if `upToBalance` is not greater than
`minBalance`. The call accepts `lowBalanceThreshold`, `lowBalanceNotified`, and `lastModified` but ignores
them. The call changes data but charges nothing. You can repeat it with the same body. Turning the top-up on
also resets the low-balance warning. The call returns the settings as the portal saved them.

`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/activeservices`. To change one entry, use

returns 404. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation has no
billing service. AI tools must be on before you turn on AI search. If it is not, the call returns 403. Turning
off AI tools also turns off AI search. If AI is turned off for the portal, turning on an AI service
returns 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. The call returns all wallet services
that are on after the change. If `service` is not a wallet service, the call returns 400. Turning a service on
does not buy it. To buy units, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`.

Returns the prices of the AI features that the portal pays for from its wallet. The list covers chat models,
embedding models, image models, and web search providers. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. It
also returns 403 if the installation has no billing service or no AI gateway. The call is read-only. Token
prices are per million tokens, and all prices are in the `currency` of the answer. Each entry has the model ID
that the AI operations take. The list does not show what the portal spent. To read the spending, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/customer/usage`. To read the models that the portal bars, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/ai-model/restrictions`.

model of `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/ai-prices` is allowed. The call returns 402 if AI tools is on but the
billing service has no customer or fails. To replace the set, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/ai-model/restrictions`.

put.description:
Replaces the whole set of AI chat models that are barred on the portal. To bar one more model, send it
together with the models already barred. To lift a restriction, leave the model out. An empty set lifts all
restrictions. First, read the current set from `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/ai-model/restrictions`. Take the
model IDs from `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/ai-prices`. If the portal has no billing customer, the call
returns 404. AI tools must be on, and you turn it on with `POST api/2.0/portal/payment/servicestate`. While AI tools
is off, the call returns 403. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. It also returns 403 if the
installation has no billing service or no AI gateway. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the
same body. The set applies from the next AI request. So an open conversation on a barred model cannot go on
with it. The call returns the stored set. If `models` is missing or has a null entry, the call returns 400.

get.description:
Returns the space that the content of the portal uses, in gigabytes rounded to two decimals. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only. The answer is a number, not an object. The portal adds up the storage counters of its
accounts. So system data that belongs to no account is not counted. To compare the result with the allowance,
use `maxTotalSize` of `GET api/2.0/portal/quota`, which is in bytes. The call does not split the space by room
or user.

200.description: The space the portal content occupies, in gigabytes rounded to two decimals

get.description:
Returns the tariff of the portal, with its state, the end of the current period, and its quotas. Any signed-in
user can call it, including a guest. Every caller gets `state`. A room admin or a DocSpace admin also gets
`dueDate` and `delayDueDate`. Only a caller with the EditPortalSettings permission gets the other fields. The
portal owner and DocSpace admins have this permission. The call is read-only and also works while the portal
is unpaid. With `refresh` set to `true`, the call reads the tariff from the billing system instead of the
cache. To see what the next period costs, use `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff/upcoming`.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description:
Whether the tariff is re-read from the billing system instead of the portal cache. The remote read is slower,
so ask for it right after a payment and leave it off for ordinary page loads.

200.description: The tariff of this portal, filled as far as the rights of the caller allow

400.description: Bad Request.

get.description:
Returns the next charges of the portal for the quotas of its tariff. The list has one entry per quota.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call is read-only and also works while the portal is unpaid. The list skips overdue quotas. It
also skips quotas without a price, such as a trial or a free plan. So the list can be empty on a portal with a
tariff. If a switch to another quota is planned, the entry shows the next quota and its quantity. With
`refresh` set to `true`, the call reads the tariff from the billing system instead of the cache.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description:
Whether the tariff is re-read from the billing system instead of the portal cache. The remote read is slower,
so ask for it right after a payment and leave it off for ordinary page loads.

200.description: The charges the portal is going to be billed next, one entry per quota, empty when nothing is due
