get.description:
Returns the quota of the portal, which is the allowance its tariff gives. It has the limits on users, paid
users, rooms, total size, and file size, and the features. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which
the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only and also works while
the portal is unpaid. Sizes are in bytes. A free or trial quota has no price. The quota shows what the portal
may use, not what it uses. The usage comes from `GET api/2.0/portal/usedspace` and
`GET api/2.0/portal/userscount`. To list the quotas the portal can switch to, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas`. To read the billing state, use `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff`.

200.description: The allowance the current tariff grants this portal, with sizes in bytes

Returns the cheapest quota that is not yearly and allows more users than the portal has active accounts.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call is read-only and buys nothing. The answer has the shape of `GET api/2.0/portal/quota`, with
sizes in bytes. If no quota fits, the call returns 200 with no quota. To list all quotas, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas`. To buy one, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/url`.

get.description:
Returns the record of the current portal, with its name, alias, owner, language, time zone, status, and dates.
Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. A caller with the EditPortalSettings permission, which the
portal owner and DocSpace admins have, gets the full record. Other callers get an object with only `tenantId`
filled. So check `tenantAlias` for null first. The call is read-only and also works while the portal is
unpaid. To read the portal settings, use `GET api/2.0/settings`. To read the tariff and the quota, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/tariff` and `GET api/2.0/portal/quota`.

200.description: The portal record, or an object in which only `tenantId` is filled when the caller has no portal-settings right

get.summary: Get a path to the portal
get.description:
Returns the absolute URL of a path on the portal, with the scheme, the current domain, and the virtual root.
Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call is read-only. It does not check the path or the
access of the caller to it. An empty `virtualPath` returns the portal root. The call adds a path that starts
with `/` to the root and resolves `~/` against the virtual root. It returns a value that starts with
`http://`, `https://`, or `mailto:` unchanged. The answer is a JSON string. It has the current domain, so
after a rename the call returns the new domain.

parameters.name: virtualPath
parameters.description:
The path to resolve. It is taken as it is: an omitted or empty value yields the portal root, a value starting
with `/` is appended to that root, a value starting with `~/` is resolved against the virtual root, and one
that already begins with `http://`, `https://` or `mailto:` is handed back unchanged. Nothing checks that the
path exists or that the caller may open it.

200.description: The absolute URL that the given portal-relative path resolves to

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Sends the portal owner an email with the links that deactivate the portal and make it active again. This call
does not change the portal. Only the portal owner can call it. Other callers get 403, including a DocSpace
admin. The call also works while the portal is unpaid. By default, a repeated call within 10 minutes of the
email sends nothing and returns 200. A later call sends a new email, and the links of earlier emails keep
working. The first link signs `PUT api/2.0/portal/suspend`, and the second signs `PUT api/2.0/portal/continue`.
By default, the first link works for 7 days, and the second never expires. To delete the portal instead, use
`POST api/2.0/portal/delete`. On a server installation, you cannot deactivate the last space. Spaces with
limited access do not count.

200.description: The request is accepted: the deactivation letter is queued and the request recorded in the audit trail, unless the same letter already went out within the repeat period; the portal itself is still active and the response carries no content

403.description: The caller is not the portal owner or has no portal-settings right

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Deactivates the portal. Its users can no longer work in it, and its rooms, files, and accounts stay. Sign the
request with the confirmation token from the first link of the email that `POST api/2.0/portal/suspend` sends.
The call also checks that the token belongs to the portal owner. Other callers get 403, including an ordinary
sign-in token. The call changes data. After it, the portal returns 404 for most calls, and a repeated call also
returns 404. To make the portal active again, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/continue` with the second link of the
email. To delete the portal for good, use `DELETE api/2.0/portal/delete`. On a server installation, you cannot
deactivate the last space. Spaces with limited access do not count.

200.description: The portal is now suspended, its users can no longer work in it and its content is kept; the response carries no content

403.description: The account the confirmation link was issued for is not the portal owner

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Sends the portal owner an email with the link that deletes the portal. This call does not change the portal.
Only the portal owner can call it. Other callers get 403, including a DocSpace admin. The call also works while
the portal is unpaid. By default, a repeated call within 10 minutes of the email sends nothing and returns 200.
A later call sends a new email, and the links of earlier emails keep working for 7 days by default. If the
portal has payments and is not on trial, the email also warns that the subscription stops renewing. The link
signs `DELETE api/2.0/portal/delete`, which deletes the portal and cannot be undone. To deactivate the portal
instead, use `POST api/2.0/portal/suspend`. On a server installation, you cannot delete the last space. Spaces
with limited access do not count.

200.description: The request is accepted, and the removal letter is queued unless one already went out within the repeat period; nothing about the portal has changed yet and the response carries no content

403.description: The caller is not the portal owner or has no portal-settings right

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

delete.description:
Deletes the portal with its rooms, files, accounts, settings, and OAuth apps. Its domain then stops serving
the portal. Sign the request with the confirmation token from the email that `POST api/2.0/portal/delete`
sends. The call also checks that the token belongs to the portal owner. Other callers get 403, including an
ordinary sign-in token. The call cannot be undone, and no operation restores the portal. To keep the content,
first start a backup with `POST api/2.0/backup/startbackup`. The call also works while the portal is unpaid.
Do not repeat it. The portal emails the owner a confirmation. The call returns the absolute URL of a feedback
form to send the owner to. To deactivate the portal instead, use `POST api/2.0/portal/suspend`. On a server
installation, you cannot delete the last space. Spaces with limited access do not count.

200.description: The absolute URL of the feedback form to send the owner of the removed portal to

403.description: The account the confirmation link was issued for is not the portal owner

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Makes a deactivated portal active again, so its users can sign in. Sign the request with the confirmation
token from the second link of the email that `POST api/2.0/portal/suspend` sends. An ordinary sign-in token
does not work here. The call changes data, and you can repeat it. An active portal stays active. The call
returns no data. To check the result, read `status` from `GET api/2.0/portal`. The call cannot bring back a
deleted portal.

200.description: The portal is active again and its users can sign in; the response carries no content

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Unblocks the portal after the retention policy blocked it for a long time without use. Its users can then sign
in again. Sign the request with the confirmation token from the unblocking link in the retention email to the
owner. An ordinary sign-in token gets 403. The call changes data and makes the portal active. It also restarts
the retention count. A repeated call returns 401. It also returns 401 for an invalid link, an earlier block's
link, or a portal that is not blocked. The call returns no data. To check the status, read `tenantStatus` from
`GET api/2.0/settings`, which a blocked portal still answers. A lapsed paid tariff stays unpaid, so renew it
next. The emails of a free portal have no such link, and support unblocks it. The call does not bring back a
deleted portal or one that its owner deactivated. To make a deactivated portal active, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/continue`.

200.description: The portal is active again and its users can sign in; the response carries no content

401.description: The unblocking link is invalid, was mailed for an earlier block, or the portal is not blocked

403.description: The call carries an ordinary sign-in token instead of the unblocking link

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns an account of the current portal by its ID, in the internal user format. Any signed-in user can read
their own profile. A DocSpace admin can read any account. A room admin can read any account except a guest
they have no relation with. A user or a guest can read only their own profile. Other callers get 403, even for
an ID that does not exist. The call is read-only. It returns 404 for an unknown ID or a system account. To
read your own profile, use `GET api/2.0/people/@self`. To get the account in the People format, with groups,
quota, and access data, use `GET api/2.0/people/{userId}`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The portal account the operation acts on, by user ID as `GET api/2.0/people` reports it. An ID belonging to
no account of this portal and an ID of an internal system account are both answered as not found.

200.description: The account of this portal, in the internal user format

403.description: The caller is not allowed to view this account: a user or a guest gets it for any ID but their own, whether the account exists or not, and a room administrator gets it for a guest they have no relation with

404.description: No account with this ID exists on the portal, or the ID belongs to a system account

get.description:
Returns an invitation URL for the role in `employeeType`, and is deprecated. Use
`POST api/2.0/portal/users/invitationlink` and the other operations under that path instead. Anyone who opens
the URL can join the portal with that role. The portal does not store the link, so you cannot list or revoke
it later. If inviting members is turned off in `GET api/2.0/settings/invitationsettings`, the call
returns 403. The caller needs the right to add users of that role. Only the portal owner gets a DocSpace admin
link. Other callers get an empty string instead of an error. The call is read-only, and you can repeat it.
Each call returns an equivalent link as a bare string. The link is signed for the calling account and has no
use limit. It expires with the email key lifetime of the portal, by default after 7 days.

parameters.name: employeeType
parameters.description:
The role whoever follows the link joins with. Only `DocSpaceAdmin`, `RoomAdmin` and `User` have a link; any
other role is refused. The portal keeps at most one link per role, so this value alone identifies it.

200.description: The invitation URL to hand to the invited person, or an empty string when the caller may not invite that role

403.description: Inviting members is disabled for the portal

400.description: Bad Request.

post.description:
Creates the invitation link of the portal for one role and returns it with the URL to share. If inviting
members is turned off in `GET api/2.0/settings/invitationsettings`, the call returns 403. The portal owner can
create a link for any role. A DocSpace admin can create the `RoomAdmin` and `User` links, and a room admin
only the `User` link. Other callers get 403. The call changes data. A role has at most one link, so a repeated
call returns 400. To change an existing link, use `PUT api/2.0/portal/users/invitationlink`. Without
`expiration`, the link never expires. Without `maxUseCount`, it has no use limit. The answer has the `id` that
the update and delete calls need. The call returns 400 for another role, an `expiration` in the past, or a
`maxUseCount` out of range. For a `RoomAdmin` or `DocSpaceAdmin` link, it returns 402 if the payment is
overdue or no paid seat is free.

schema.description: The role a new invitation link grants, and the limits placed on it.

200.description: The invitation link as it was created, with the `id` to address it later and the `url` to share

400.description: The request body cannot be read, the role is not `DocSpaceAdmin`, `RoomAdmin` or `User`, the use limit is outside 1-1000, the deadline is in the past, or the role already has a link

402.description: The link is for a paying role, and the portal payment is overdue or the portal quota has no free paid seat left

403.description: Inviting members is disabled for the portal, the caller has no right to add users of that role, or a non-owner asks for the DocSpace administrator link

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Changes the deadline and the use limit of an invitation link by its `id`. The call applies the whole body. So a
missing `expiration` removes the deadline, and a missing `maxUseCount` removes the use limit. You cannot change
the role of a link. To do this, delete the link and create a new one. If inviting members is turned off in
`GET api/2.0/settings/invitationsettings`, the call returns 403. The portal owner can change every link. A
DocSpace admin can change the `RoomAdmin` and `User` links, and a room admin only the `User` link. Other
callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. It keeps the use count of the
link. After `expiration` passes, a repeated call returns 400. The call returns the whole link as it now stands.
If no link has this `id`, the call returns 404. The call returns 400 for an `expiration` in the past or a
`maxUseCount` out of range. It also returns 400 if `maxUseCount` is lower than the `currentUseCount` of the
link.

schema.description: The invitation link being changed, with the deadline and use limit it is to have afterwards.

200.description: The invitation link as it now stands, with the deadline and the use limit that were applied

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `id`, the use limit is outside 1-1000 or lower than the number of uses the link already has, or the deadline is in the past

403.description: Inviting members is disabled for the portal, the caller has no right to add users of the link's role, or a non-owner tries to change the DocSpace administrator link

delete.description:
Deletes an invitation link of the portal by its `id`. Its URL then stops letting anyone join, and the accounts
that joined through it stay. If inviting members is turned off in `GET api/2.0/settings/invitationsettings`,
the call returns 403. The portal owner can delete every link. A DocSpace admin can delete the `RoomAdmin` and
`User` links, and a room admin only the `User` link. Other callers get 403. The call cannot be undone. A
repeated call or an unknown `id` returns 404. A body without `id` returns 400. A new link for the role gets a
new `id` and URL, and its use count starts from zero. To create it, use
`POST api/2.0/portal/users/invitationlink`. To stop invitations and keep the links, turn inviting off with
`PUT api/2.0/settings/invitationsettings`. The links then stop working until you turn it on again.

schema.description: Which invitation link is withdrawn.

200.description: The invitation link is deleted and its URL no longer lets anyone join the portal

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `id`

403.description: Inviting members is disabled for the portal, the caller has no right to add users of the link's role, or a non-owner tries to delete the DocSpace administrator link

404.description: No invitation link with this ID exists on the portal

read every link. A DocSpace admin can read the `RoomAdmin` and `User` links, and a room admin only the `User`
link. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. If the role has no link yet, the call returns 200 with no
link. To create one, use `POST api/2.0/portal/users/invitationlink`. The call returns 400 for a role other
than `DocSpaceAdmin`, `RoomAdmin`, or `User`. For a `RoomAdmin` or `DocSpaceAdmin` link, it returns 402 if the
payment is overdue or no paid seat is free. It returns 402 even when the role has no link.

Returns how many accounts of the portal have the active status, of every user type. Disabled and deleted
accounts are not counted. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace
admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The answer is a number, not an object. To compare
it with the allowance, use `countUser` and `countPaidUser` of `GET api/2.0/portal/quota`. To list the accounts
or filter them by type, group, or status, use `GET api/2.0/people/filter`.

post.summary: Mark a gift message as read
post.description:
Marks the open-source gift message as read for the calling user, so the app stops showing it. Any signed-in
user can call it. The portal saves the flag per user, so other accounts still see the message. The call
changes data, and you can repeat it. It returns success even if saving fails. In that case, it only writes the
error to the portal log. So a success does not prove that the portal saved the flag. No operation reads the
flag or clears it again.

200.description: The gift message is marked as read for the calling user; the same answer is returned when saving the flag failed, because the error is only written to the portal log. The response carries no content

post.description:
Sends the welcome email of a newly registered portal to the account in `userid`. Anyone can call it without
signing in. Instead of a token, `key` must be the confirmation key of the sign-in link for that account. The
key works for one hour. The call returns 403 for a wrong, foreign, or expired key, and then sends nothing. The
call changes data. Call it once, right after registration. Each repeated call with a valid key sends the emails
again. On a hosted portal, the password link of the earlier email then stops working. If the installation
requires SMS or an authenticator app after registration, the call turns that method on for the portal. It skips
this step for an internal test address. On a hosted portal in custom mode, the call also sends the registration
data to the sales address. The call returns no data.

parameters.name: userid
parameters.description:
The account the welcome letter is addressed to, by portal user ID. The key in `key` has to have been issued
for this same account, so the pair is what authorises the call.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description:
The confirmation key from the sign-in link the portal issued for that account, which stands in for a token
here. It is accepted for one hour after it was created; a wrong, foreign or expired key answers 403 and sends
nothing.

200.description: The welcome letters were sent and the configured second factor was switched on for the portal

403.description: The confirmation key does not match the user or is older than one hour

Sets whether the portal blocks the developer tools for the user type `user`. The tools are API keys, OAuth
apps, and webhooks. Room admins and DocSpace admins keep access. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission,
which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data. You can repeat
it with the same body. The change applies to all users immediately. It returns the saved setting.

Returns whether the portal blocks the developer tools for the user type `user`. The tools are API keys, OAuth
apps, and webhooks. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call is read-only. To change the
setting, use `POST api/2.0/settings/devtoolsaccess`.

get.description:
Returns the active connections of the calling user on this portal.
Each item is a sign-in from the last year that is still active.
Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest.
The list never shows other users' connections, even to a DocSpace admin.
The call is read-only.
Items come newest first.
If the request has a portal cookie, its connection comes first.
That item shows the browser, platform, IP address, and location of this request.
The `loginEvent` field holds the ID of that connection.
Without the cookie, for example with a token in the `Authorization` header, `loginEvent` is 0.
Then, if the user has no active connections, the list has one item for this request.
To end one connection, pass its `id` to `PUT api/2.0/security/activeconnections/logout/{loginEventId}`.

200.description: The caller's active connections, newest sign-in first, with `loginEvent` pointing at the connection the request itself was made with

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Ends all active connections of the calling user and returns a link to set a new password.
Use it after a suspicious sign-in.
Any signed-in user can call it for their own account, including a guest.

The account stays active, and the password stays valid.

changed, deleted, shared, or set. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and
DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. In a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the login
history and audit trail section is turned off. The call is read-only. It looks back
only as far as the audit trail lifetime of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/settings/lifetime`. In `actionText`,
the call cuts every inserted value to 50 characters. An empty list means the portal recorded no audit events
in that period. To filter by user, module, action, or period, use `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/filter`.

get.description:
Returns the audit events of the portal that match the query filters, newest first. You can filter by user,
module, action, action type, entry type, target, and period. An omitted filter matches everything. Requires
the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403.
Without the audit option of the pricing plan, the call ignores the filters. It then returns the 20 most
recent events. In a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the login history and audit trail section is turned
off. The call is read-only. To get the filter values, use `GET api/2.0/security/audit/types` and
`GET api/2.0/security/audit/mappers`. If `action` is set, the call matches only that action and ignores
`moduleType` and `actionType`. With `action`, the call matches `target` exactly. With `entryType`, it keeps
the events whose `target` contains the value. It ignores `entryType` without `target`, and `target` without
`action` or `entryType`. The call applies the filters first and the page
window after them. So a full page means more matching events may exist, and there is no total count. The audit
trail lifetime does not limit this call. Without `from`, it returns events back to the oldest one the portal
stores. The call returns 400 for a parameter of the wrong type, a `count` out of range, or an invalid date.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The user who performed the action, given by portal user ID. Leave it at the empty GUID to keep the events of
every user.

parameters.name: moduleType
parameters.description:
The module the recorded action belongs to, spelled as `GET api/2.0/security/audit/types` lists it under
`moduleTypes`. `GET api/2.0/security/audit/mappers` shows which module records which action. The default
value keeps every module.

parameters.name: actionType
parameters.description:
The kind of change the action made, spelled as `GET api/2.0/security/audit/types` lists it under
`actionTypes`. The default value keeps every kind.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
The exact action recorded, spelled as the `messageAction` of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/mappers`. Naming
one narrows the answer to that single action and overrides `moduleType` and `actionType`, which stop
narrowing anything once it is set.

parameters.name: entryType
parameters.description:
The kind of object the action was performed on, spelled as `GET api/2.0/security/audit/types` lists it under
`entryTypes`. Pair it with `target` to filter by object without pinning a single action.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description:
The object the action was performed on, as the audit trail recorded it - a file name, a user account, a room
title. It is matched in full and exactly as stored, so it narrows the answer only when `action` or
`entryType` is set as well.

parameters.description:

come back is in the portal time zone instead, so the two do not line up on a portal that is not on UTC.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The latest moment an event may have been recorded at, read as a UTC instant in the same way as `from`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:

to ask for them; a full page means there may be further matches beyond it.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
How many matching events to skip before the page begins, counting from the newest. Advance it by `count` to
walk backwards through the trail.

post.description:
Starts a background job that builds an audit trail report of the portal, and returns the job state. Requires
the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. In
a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the pricing plan has no audit option. It also returns 402 if the
login history and audit trail section is turned off. Without `from` and `to`, the report covers the audit trail
lifetime of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/settings/lifetime`, up to now. The
call moves an earlier `from` to the start of the lifetime and a future `to` to now. It ignores the other
filters of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/filter`. The call queues work. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/report` until `isCompleted` is true. The portal saves the file in the
caller's My documents section. An XLSX report keeps at most 200,000 of the most recent events by default, and
fewer for long events. Its header says how many events it left out. A CSV report has every event of the
period. If a CSV file is too large for the editor, `resultFileUrl` downloads it instead of opening it. Each
caller has one job per report kind. While the job runs, a repeated call returns that job and starts no second
one. After the job ends, a repeated call builds a new file. To cancel the job, use
`DELETE api/2.0/security/audit/events/report`. The call returns 400 if the period ends before it starts or
lies entirely outside the lifetime.

text file.

parameters.name: to

`POST api/2.0/security/audit/events/report`. Repeat it until `isCompleted` is true. Requires the

delete.description:
Cancels the caller's audit trail report job and removes it from the queue. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. In a cloud installation,
the call returns 402 if the pricing plan has no audit option. It also returns 402 if the login history and
audit trail section is turned off. The call queues the cancellation for the service that builds reports. So a
200 response means that the service got the request, not that the job has stopped. To check, repeat
`GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/report` until it returns an empty answer. The call affects only the
caller's own audit trail report. To cancel the login history report, use
`DELETE api/2.0/security/audit/login/report`. You can repeat the call, and a call with no running job is not
an error. A job cancelled before it saved the file leaves nothing in My documents. To build the report again,
use `POST api/2.0/security/audit/events/report`.

than the login history lifetime. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and
DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. In a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the login history
and audit trail section is turned off. The call does not need the audit option of the pricing plan. The call
is read-only. The audit trail lifetime sets how far `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/last` and the audit
trail report look back. The login history lifetime does the same for the login history report. The audit
trail lifetime deletes no events and does not limit `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/filter`. The
installation decides how long it stores audit events. To change the lifetimes, use
`POST api/2.0/security/audit/settings/lifetime`.

Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. In a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the pricing plan has no audit option. It also
returns 402 if the login history and audit trail section is turned off. The call changes data and replaces

values, use `GET api/2.0/security/audit/settings/lifetime`. You can repeat the call with the same body. The
change takes effect immediately for `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/last` and for both reports. A shorter
login history lifetime lets the daily cleanup permanently delete older login events. A shorter audit trail
lifetime deletes nothing. Older audit events stay in `GET api/2.0/security/audit/events/filter`. They return
to the recent events and the report when the lifetime grows. The call
returns 400 if the body has no `settings` or a lifetime is outside 1 to 180 days. It then saves neither value.

post.description:
Starts a background job that builds a login history report of the portal, and returns the job state. Requires
the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. In
a cloud installation, the call returns 402 if the pricing plan has no audit option. It also returns 402 if the
login history and audit trail section is turned off. Without `from` and `to`, the report covers the login
history lifetime of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/settings/lifetime`, up to now.
The call moves an earlier `from` to the start of the lifetime and a future `to` to now. It ignores the other
filters of `GET api/2.0/security/audit/login/filter`. The call queues work. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/security/audit/login/report` until `isCompleted` is true. The portal saves the file in the
caller's My documents section. An XLSX report keeps at most 200,000 of the most recent events by default, and
fewer for long events. Its header says how many events it left out. A CSV report has every event of the
period. If a CSV file is too large for the editor, `resultFileUrl` downloads it instead of opening it. Each
caller has one job per report kind. While the job runs, a repeated call returns that job and starts no second
one. After the job ends, a repeated call builds a new file. To cancel the job, use
`DELETE api/2.0/security/audit/login/report`. The call returns 400 if the period ends before it starts or lies
entirely outside the lifetime.

text file.

carries the user ID, name, and email, and the portal ID and address. It also says if the caller is a DocSpace
admin or a guest. Last, it says if the developer tools setting opens OAuth2 apps to all users. Send the token
to the identity service in the `x-signature` header. This API does not accept it instead of the token of
`POST api/2.0/authentication`. The call is read-only and returns the token as a plain string. Request a new
token before each exchange instead of storing it.

no settings of its own and uses those of the installation. A standalone installation then returns its values,
and a cloud portal returns empty fields. The password in `credentialsUserPassword` is always empty. So ask the
user for it before you save the settings again. To check that the mail server accepts mail, use
`GET api/2.0/smtpsettings/smtp/test`.

Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. If the SMTP settings section is turned off for the portal, the call returns 402. The call changes
data. You can repeat it with the same body. The portal uses the new settings for its next email. The call does not
connect to `host` or check the settings. To check them, use `GET api/2.0/smtpsettings/smtp/test` after this
call. If `port` is omitted, the portal saves `25`. The call does not save `useNtlm`, so the portal never signs
in with NTLM. It returns the saved settings with an empty password. The call returns 400 if `host` or
`senderAddress` is empty, or `senderDisplayName` is missing. It also returns 400 if `enableAuth` is true and
`credentialsUserName` or `credentialsUserPassword` is empty. It also returns 400 if a text field is too long or
`port` is out of range. Nothing is saved after a 400. To return to the settings of the installation, use
`DELETE api/2.0/smtpsettings/smtp`.

the cookie section, the call returns the default pair instead of the stored one. The `cookieSettingsEnabled`
field of `GET api/2.0/settings` has the same flag without the number. To change the pair, use

post.description:
Starts the free Docs Connect trial for the current portal. If the trial is granted, the call adds the assigned
Docs Connect server to the Content Security Policy settings. To check the subscriptions and the tariff state
first, use `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff`. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and
DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and a repeated call returns 400. It
returns `true` if the trial is granted. It returns `false` if the billing service declines it, for example
after an earlier trial. Then nothing changes. It also returns `false` if the billing service does not answer,
or the portal cannot read its answer. Then the trial may be granted. So check `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff` with
`refresh=true` before you call again. The call never buys a paid plan. To move a paid Docs Connect
subscription to Docs Connect Dev Pack, use `POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/switchtodevpack`. The call returns
400 if the portal already has a Docs Connect trial, Docs Connect, or Docs Connect Dev Pack. It returns 402 if
the tariff is delayed or not paid. It returns 403 if the billing service is not configured. If the
installation has no Docs Connect trial quota, the call returns 404. After a granted trial, the call returns
403 if the server address makes the Content Security Policy header too long. The trial then stays granted.

post.summary: Switch Docs Connect to Docs Connect Dev Pack
post.description:
Switches the paid Docs Connect subscription of the current portal to Docs Connect Dev Pack for `quantity` users.
The call charges the price difference to the portal wallet and moves the license to the new product. To check
the subscriptions and the tariff state first, use `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff`. To get the price, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/calculatedevpack` with the same `quantity`. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other
callers get 403. The call spends money, and a repeated call returns 400. Concurrent calls run one after
another, so the portal charges the wallet once. It returns `true` if the subscription is switched. It returns
`false` if the billing service declines the switch. Then the portal charges nothing and stays on Docs Connect.
It also returns `false` if the billing service does not answer, or the portal cannot read its answer. Then the
switch may be done. So check `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff` with `refresh=true` before you call again. To change
the number of users, or to return to Docs Connect at the next billing period, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/updatewallet`. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read. It also returns 400
without an active Docs Connect subscription. It also returns 400 if the portal already has Docs Connect Dev Pack, or
`quantity` is below its minimum. It returns 402 if the tariff is delayed or not paid. It returns 403 if the
billing service is not configured. It returns 404 for a portal without a billing customer, or an installation
without these wallet products.

Calculates the price of switching the portal from Docs Connect to Docs Connect Dev Pack for `quantity` users.
The call changes nothing and charges nothing. To check the subscriptions and the tariff state first, use
`GET api/2.0/portal/tariff`. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only, so you
can try several values of `quantity` before the switch. An empty result means that the billing service cannot
price the switch. In that case, do not start the switch. To switch, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/switchtodevpack` with the same `quantity`. It needs no value from this
response. To price a new number of users for an existing subscription, use
`PUT api/2.0/portal/payment/calculatewallet`. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read, or the portal
has no active Docs Connect subscription. It also returns 400 if the portal already has Docs Connect Dev Pack,
or `quantity` is below its minimum. It returns 402 if the tariff is delayed or not paid. It returns 403 if the
billing service is not configured. It returns 404 for a portal without a billing customer, or an installation
without these wallet products.

Returns the Docs Connect tenant of the current portal. It describes the Docs Connect server assigned to the
portal. It also gives the subscription end date and the payment. A tenant exists only after a Docs Connect

permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The
portal caches the tenant for an hour, and the absence of a tenant for a minute. So after a subscription change,
pass `refresh=true` to read the current state from Docs Connect. The `address` field is the full address of
the server. The dates in the result are in UTC. An empty result means that the portal has no Docs Connect
tenant yet. This is a normal state, not an error. So use this call to check if Docs Connect is active. To read
the license, the configuration, the user quota, or the usage, use `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/info`,
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/config`, `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota`, or
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/usage`. Each of them returns 400 while the portal has no tenant.

Returns the Docs Connect license of the current portal, its server, and the user limits of the license. It
also returns the editor and viewer usage of the current period. The portal needs a Docs Connect tenant from
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/trial` or a Docs Connect purchase. Without one, the call returns 400, and
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant` returns an empty result. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission,
which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The portal
caches the answer for a minute. So after a subscription change, pass
`refresh=true` to read the current state from Docs Connect. If the portal has a paid Docs Connect or Docs
Connect Dev Pack subscription, `license.trial` is `false`. This holds even when the license itself is a trial.
The dates in the result are in UTC. For one total of active users without the split by role, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/usage`. To read the configuration, the users counted, or the server
address, use `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/config`, `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota`,
or `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant`.

get.summary: Get the Docs Connect tenant configuration
get.description:
Returns the configuration of the Docs Connect tenant of the current portal. It includes the tenant name, the
security secret and header, the server file size limit, and anonymous access. It also includes the WOPI switch
and the IP filter rules. The portal needs a Docs Connect tenant from `POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/trial`
or a Docs Connect purchase. Without one, the call returns 400, and `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant`
returns an empty result. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace
admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The portal caches the answer for an hour. To read
the current state from Docs Connect, pass `refresh=true`. An update with
`PUT api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/config` clears the cached copy, so the next read needs no refresh. The
`security.secret` field is a credential, so treat the response as sensitive. An empty or missing
`ipFilter.rules` means that no address is restricted. To read the license, the server address, the users
counted, or the usage, use `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/info`, `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant`,
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota`, or `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/usage`.

put.summary: Update the Docs Connect tenant configuration

Replaces the configuration of the Docs Connect tenant of the current portal. It returns the configuration as
Docs Connect stored it. The portal needs a Docs Connect tenant from `POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/trial` or
a Docs Connect purchase. Without one, the call returns 400, and `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant`
returns an empty result. First read the current values with `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/config`.
Then send back whole sections: `security`, `server`, `wopi`, and `ipFilter`. Sections you leave out do not
reach Docs Connect. In a section you send, an unset field becomes `0`, `false`, or empty. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call
changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. The next read returns the new values without
`refresh=true`. The call changes only these settings, never the subscription, the user quota, or the license.
It returns 400 if the body cannot be read, a text is too long, or `server.fileSizeLimit` is out of range. In
that case, nothing reaches Docs Connect.

Returns the Docs Connect user quota of the current portal. It lists the users who count as Docs Connect editors
and as viewers, and when each entry expires. The portal needs a Docs Connect tenant from
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/trial` or a Docs Connect purchase. Without one, the call returns 400, and
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant` returns an empty result. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission,
which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only, and the portal
caches the answer for a minute. To read the current state from Docs Connect, pass `refresh=true`. The `users`
list holds the editors, and `usersView` holds the viewers, in no particular order. For a portal member,
`userId` is the DocSpace user ID. For anyone else, it is an ID of Docs Connect. The `expire` value is a UTC
date and time as a string. Empty lists mean that no user is counted yet. For the license limits and the totals
by role, use `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/info`. For one total of active users, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/usage`. To get the same lists as an "xlsx" file, use

Starts a background job that saves the Docs Connect user quota of the current portal as an "xlsx" file. The
portal saves the file in the "My documents" folder of the caller. The report lists the editors and viewers with
the type and expiration date of each. It also sums up the internal, external, and remaining users against the
license limits. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. The call does not check for a Docs Connect tenant. Without one, the job fails and puts
the reason in `error`. The call queues work. Repeat `GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota/report` until
`isCompleted` is true. Then take the file from `resultFileId` or `resultFileUrl`. To cancel a running job, use
`DELETE api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota/report`. Each caller has one report job at a time. While it
runs, a repeated call returns that job and starts no second one. After the job ends, a repeated call builds a
new report and saves another file. A new job comes back with `percentage` 0, not the report. The report shows
the quota at the moment of the build, and its file name has the build date. To read the same data as JSON, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota`.

Returns the state of the Docs Connect user quota report that the caller started with
`POST api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota/report`. It shows only the caller's own job, never a report of
another admin. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until `isCompleted` is true.
The job also completes on failure, so then check `error`. It is empty if the report was built, and holds the
failure message otherwise. The report file also stays in the "My documents" folder of the caller. An empty
result means that the caller has no job. Either none was started, it was cancelled, or the portal deleted its
state. The portal keeps the state of a finished job for a day, and a new report deletes it. This is a normal
state, not an error. To cancel a report, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/docscloud/tenant/quota/report`.

Starts encryption of the local storage of the installation, or decryption if the data is already encrypted. The
saved encryption state sets the direction. The run covers all portals of the installation. First, reset a
third-party storage with `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage` and a CDN with `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access space. The call
queues work and deletes the backup schedules of all portals. Every portal stays unavailable until the run ends.
Repeat `GET api/2.0/settings/encryption/progress` until it returns 100. During a run, a repeated call returns
403. After the run, a repeated call starts the opposite run. The server generates the password and never
returns it. To email every user before the portals go down, set `notifyUsers` to true. The call returns `true`
when the run is queued. In a custom build, it returns `false` and starts nothing. The call returns 415 if the
installation does not offer encryption. It also returns 415 if the current portal uses a third-party storage
or CDN. Start it only when no portal runs a backup. If the portal is not paid, the call returns 402.

to 100. To start a run, use `POST api/2.0/settings/encryption/start`. To see its direction, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/encryption/settings`. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. This is the

run ends. After that, and when no run exists, the response is empty. So poll at least once a minute. In a custom

get.description:
Returns the greeting title of the current portal as a plain string. The portal shows it as the welcome heading
on the sign-in page and keeps it as the portal name. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The
call is read-only. The answer is never empty. If the portal has no title, the call returns the built-in
default caption in the language of the caller. So the answer cannot tell a saved title from the
default one. To check that, use `GET api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings/isdefault`. The `greetingSettings`
field of `GET api/2.0/settings` has the same string. The title is not the portal address or the white-label
logo text. To read the logo text, use `GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logotext`.

Replaces the greeting title of the current portal with `title` and stores it as the portal name. An empty
`title` clears the title. Then the portal shows the built-in default caption, and
`GET api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings/isdefault` returns `true`. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission,
which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and the new
title applies immediately to every user of the portal. You can repeat it with the same body. On a free or
trial cloud plan, the call checks the title against the character rule of the installation. A paid cloud plan
and a server installation skip this check. The call returns a localized confirmation message, not the stored
title. To read the title, use `GET api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings`. The call returns 400 if `title` is
missing, too long, or breaks the character rule.

signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call is read-only. It returns `true` while the portal
stores no title, and `false` after a non-empty title is saved. The portal stores no title after an empty

installation configures no portal name. For a missing title, `GET api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings` returns
the default caption. So only this call tells the default greeting from a custom title with the same words.
The answer covers only the greeting title. To check the white-label logos and logo text, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/isdefault` and `GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logotext/isdefault`.

Resets the greeting title of the current portal to the portal name configured for the installation. If the
installation configures no name, the stored title becomes empty. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission,
which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and the change
applies immediately to every user of the portal. You can repeat it, and a second call changes nothing. It
returns the title in force after the reset. For an empty title, it returns the localized default caption.
Then `GET api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings/isdefault` returns `true`. The call does not reset the portal
logos or the white-label logo text. To reset them, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/restore` and
`PUT api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logotext/restore`. To set a custom title, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/greetingsettings`.

get.description:
Returns the IP restriction list of the current portal, the addresses allowed to reach it. Each entry has its `id`
and the `forAdmin` flag. An entry with `forAdmin` admits only DocSpace admins. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only and
honours `If-None-Match`. The list has no defined order. On a portal without restrictions, the list is empty, and
an empty list blocks nobody. The portal owner and the installation's own networks are never blocked. If it holds
the `ETag` of an earlier answer, unchanged addresses return 304 with an empty body. The `ETag` covers only the
addresses, so a change of `forAdmin` alone also returns 304. To check whether the restrictions are enforced, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions/settings`. To replace the whole list, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions`. It takes addresses, not the IDs returned here. You cannot add or delete a
single entry.

put.description:
Replaces the whole IP restriction list of the current portal and stores the enforcement flag. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call
changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. It deletes every stored entry that the body does not
repeat. The new list applies to new requests immediately. An omitted `enable` is on for a list with addresses and
off for an empty one. The call returns 400 if the body has no `ipRestrictions` or `enable` is `true` with an empty
list. It also returns 400 if an entry is not a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Ranges and CIDR blocks also
return 400. The portal owner and the installation's own networks are never blocked. So a DocSpace admin who leaves
out their own address locks themselves out. The answer echoes the request, so it has no entry IDs, and an omitted
`enable` stays empty. To read the stored list, use `GET api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions`.

Returns whether the IP restrictions of the current portal are enforced, and when the setting last changed.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call is read-only and honours `If-Modified-Since`. If it holds the `Last-Modified` of an earlier

`false`. A `true` flag blocks nothing while the address list is empty. To read the addresses, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions`. The installation configuration can also turn enforcement off for all its
portals. The portal owner and the installation's own networks are never blocked. To change the flag, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions/settings`. It also replaces the address list, so resend the addresses in
force.

with an empty list. It also returns 400 if an entry is not a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Ranges and CIDR blocks
also return 400. The portal owner and the installation's own networks are never blocked. So a DocSpace admin who
leaves out their own address locks themselves out. The answer echoes the request, so it has no entry IDs, and an
omitted `enable` stays empty. To read the stored list, use `GET api/2.0/settings/iprestrictions`.

get.description:
Re-reads the license file of this Enterprise installation and applies its quota and tariff to the portal. So a
replaced file or a renewed license takes effect without a restart. If a file was staged by
`POST api/2.0/settings/license`, the call activates it. For the first activation, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/license/accept` instead. Any signed-in user can call it. Despite the `GET`, the call
changes data. You can repeat it, and each call applies the same license again. The call returns `true` when
it applied the license. It returns `false` and changes nothing on a SaaS or open-source installation, which
has no license path. The call returns 402 if the file is missing, cannot be read, or has no customer id or
signature. It also returns 402 if the editing service does not confirm the license or reports another one. If
the license starts later, the call returns 400. The call works while the portal is unpaid.

200.description: `true` when the license file was re-read and the portal quota and tariff rewritten from it, `false` on an installation that has no license path configured

400.description: The license file does not start until a later date

402.description: No license file is on disk, the file cannot be read as a license or carries no customer id or signature, or the editing service does not confirm it

post.description:
Activates the license file staged by `POST api/2.0/settings/license` on this Enterprise installation. The
call makes the staged file the active one and applies its quota and tariff to the portal. Without a staged
file, it applies the active license file again. Any signed-in user can call it. The call changes data, and
you can repeat it. Read the result from the body, not from the status code. An empty string means the license
is now active. Any other string is a message that explains why the activation failed. The call returns such a
message for a missing or incorrect file, or a license the editing service rejects. It also returns a message
if the license starts later. The call records the acceptance of the license even if the activation
fails. On a SaaS or open-source installation, the call changes nothing. It returns a message that the pricing
plan does not support the option. The call works while the portal is unpaid.

get.description:
Returns whether this installation still needs a license file. The setup wizard asks
this before it offers to upload a license. Anyone can call it without signing in. The call is read-only. It
returns `true` only for an Enterprise installation whose license file is not on disk yet. It returns `false`
on a SaaS or open-source installation, which needs no license. It also returns `false` if the portal lets
anyone in without an account, or hides the pricing section. The same applies to an installation set up from
cloud image metadata. So `false` does not mean that the portal has a license. The call does not describe the
active license or check it with the editing service. The answer becomes `false` only after a staged file is
activated, not after the upload. To activate it, use `POST api/2.0/settings/license/accept`. The call works
while the portal is unpaid.

200.description: `true` when this Enterprise installation still needs a license file, `false` when one is already active or the build needs none

post.description:
Uploads a license file for this Enterprise installation as `multipart/form-data` and stages it. The call reads
only the first entry of `Files` and ignores the rest. It checks the file but does not activate it. To activate
it, use `POST api/2.0/settings/license/accept`. Until then, the portal keeps its current license. Requires a
DocSpace admin, or a wizard or admin link token before the setup wizard is complete. Other callers get 403,
including such a token after the wizard is complete. The call changes data. A
new upload replaces the staged file, so you can repeat it. The call returns a localized text that you can show
to the user. For a license past its due date, the text adds the date when support and updates ended. The call
still accepts such a license. The call returns 400 if the request has no file or the license starts
later. It returns 415 on a SaaS or open-source installation, which takes no license file. The editing service
checks the license only at activation.

files.description:
The license file, sent as `multipart/form-data`. Only the first entry is read and the rest are ignored, and a
request carrying none is refused with 400. A file that cannot be read as a license, that carries no customer
id or signature, or that was issued for the other edition fails the call; one whose start date has not
arrived yet is refused, while one already past its due date is still accepted. Staging only stores the file -
`POST api/2.0/settings/license/accept` puts it in force - and a file staged earlier is overwritten.

put.description:
Updates the brute-force protection of the portal sign-in. After `attemptCount` failed attempts within
`checkPeriod` seconds, the portal blocks the sign-in for `blockTime` seconds. The call replaces all three values
together. So to change one value, first read the others with `GET api/2.0/settings/security/loginsettings`.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. The new values apply to attempts made
after this call. Running counters and blocks stay as they are. The portal counts failed attempts per user name and
IP address. So one blocked member does not block the rest of the portal. A blocked pair cannot sign in even with
the correct password. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read, or a value is missing or out of range. It
returns the stored settings and whether they match the defaults.

get.description:
Returns the brute-force protection of the portal sign-in. It has the tolerated failed attempts, the counting
window, and the block time. The window and the block time are in seconds. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. It
supports `If-Modified-Since` with the `Last-Modified` value of an earlier answer. If the settings have not changed
since then, the call returns 304 with an empty body. A portal that nobody configured allows 5 failed attempts in
60 seconds and blocks for 60 seconds. Then `isDefault` is `true`, and it becomes `false` when any of the three
values differs. The answer does not show which accounts or addresses are blocked now. To read past lockouts in the
login history, use `GET api/2.0/security/audit/login/filter`. To change the values, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/security/loginsettings`. To restore the defaults, use
`DELETE api/2.0/settings/security/loginsettings`.

delete.description:
Resets the brute-force protection of the portal sign-in to the defaults. The defaults are 5 failed attempts, a
window of 60 seconds, and a block of 60 seconds. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal
owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data and takes no parameters. It
overwrites the current values without a confirmation. To keep them, first read them with
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/loginsettings`. You can repeat the call. The reset applies to attempts made after
this call. Sign-ins that are already blocked stay blocked until their block ends. Running attempt counters stay as
they are. The sign-in form asks for a captcha one attempt before the block. The call returns the restored settings
with `isDefault` set to `true`. To set your own values, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/security/loginsettings`.

post.description:
Turns on or off the contact form of the sign-in page for visitors who cannot get into the portal. The form
sends their message to the DocSpace admins. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner
and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. Send `turnOn` as `true` to show the form, or `false` to hide
it. The change covers the whole portal and applies to the next sign-in page. The call changes data, and you
can repeat it with the same body. It returns a localized confirmation message, not the stored flag. To read
the flag without signing in, use `GET api/2.0/settings` and its `enableAdmMess` field. That field is also
`true` while the portal's payment has lapsed, even if the form is turned off here. The form sends messages
with `POST api/2.0/settings/sendadmmail`. This setting does not change the notifications that admins get as
portal members. To subscribe to those, use `POST api/2.0/settings/notification`.

post.summary: Send a message to the administrator
post.description:
Sends a message to the DocSpace admins from someone who cannot get into the portal. This is the contact form
of the sign-in page. First, turn the form on with `POST api/2.0/settings/messagesettings`. While the portal's
payment has lapsed, the form works without that. The `enableAdmMess` field of `GET api/2.0/settings` shows
whether the form works. Anyone can call it without signing in. The call returns 400 if `email` is not a valid
address or `message` is empty without its markup.
If the caller is not signed in and the installation has a CAPTCHA, `recaptchaResponse` must carry a solved
challenge. If it is missing or not accepted, the call returns 403. The call queues the letter to the admins
subscribed to admin notifications. So a success means that the portal accepted the message, not that anyone
read it. It returns a localized confirmation message. Do not repeat it, since each call sends another letter.
The portal limits attempts per network address. More attempts return 429.

Sends an email with a join link to the address in the request. This is the self-registration behind the
register link of the sign-in page. First, the portal needs a trusted-domain policy, which
`POST api/2.0/settings/maildomainsettings` saves. Without one, the call returns 405 to every caller. The
`enabledJoin` field of `GET api/2.0/settings` shows whether the portal has such a policy. Anyone can call it
without signing in. The call returns 400 if `email` is not a valid ASCII address or already belongs to a
member. It also returns 400 if the address is outside the trusted domains of the policy. The invitee becomes a
member only after following the link. The trusted-domain settings make the new member a user or a room admin.
When the portal's paid places are taken, the new member is always a user. If the installation limits
invitations, each sent email spends one of `invitationLimit`. A success returns a localized confirmation
message. Do not repeat the call. Each call sends another email.

get.description:
Returns whether one kind of notification is turned on for the calling user. Set the kind in the route `type`.
Kinds 0 and 1 are the new-item badges and the room activity letters. Kinds 2 and 3 are the daily feed digest
and the tips letters. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call is read-only and reads only
the caller's own settings. Badges are on by default. Kinds 1, 2, and 3 are off until
`POST api/2.0/settings/notification` turns them on. The call returns 400 if `type` is not one of these kinds.
To list the muted rooms, use `GET api/2.0/settings/notification/rooms`. To list the delivery channels, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/notification/channels`.

parameters.name: type

post.description:
Turns one kind of notification on or off for the calling user. Kinds 0 and 1 of `type` are the new-item badges
and the room activity letters. Kinds 2 and 3 are the daily feed digest and the tips letters. Any signed-in
user can call it, including a guest. It changes data only in the caller's own settings. You can repeat it
with the same body. With badges off, the Files responses show `new` as 0 and mark files as muted. With room
activity off, the hourly room digest and immediate room letters, such as mentions, stop. Turning off
kind 2 or 3 stops the daily digest or the tips letters. The call returns the request as sent, not the stored
state. If `type` is not one of these kinds, the call stores nothing but still returns it. So check the result
with `GET api/2.0/settings/notification/{type}`. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read or has no
`type`. To mute a single room, use `POST api/2.0/settings/notification/rooms`.

200.description: The notification kind and state as they were sent in the request

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `type`

get.description:
Returns the IDs of the rooms the calling user has muted, as `disabledRooms`. Any signed-in user can call it,
including a guest. The call is read-only and reads only the caller's own list. An empty list means no room is
muted. The list is in the order the rooms were added, without paging. It holds the IDs as
`POST api/2.0/settings/notification/rooms` stored them. So it can hold numeric portal room IDs and string IDs
of third-party rooms. An ID stays in the list after its room is deleted. For a muted room, the portal leaves
its activity out of the hourly room digest and the daily feed. It also skips that room's immediate letters.
The Files responses hide its new-item counters. Muting a room changes nothing for its other members. To turn
whole kinds of notification on or off, use `POST api/2.0/settings/notification`.

200.description: The identifiers of the rooms the calling user has silenced

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Mutes or unmutes one room for the calling user. Set `mute` to true to mute the room, or to false to unmute it.
Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. It changes data only in the caller's own list. One call
changes one room. A repeated call with the same body changes nothing. Name the room in `roomsId`, as a numeric
portal room ID or a string ID of a third-party room. The call checks neither that the room exists nor that the
caller can access it. So it stores a mistyped ID as sent. For a muted room, the portal leaves its activity out
of the hourly room digest and the daily feed. It also skips that room's immediate letters. The Files responses
hide its new-item counters. They stop offering the `mute` action on rooms when badges, room activity, and the
daily feed are all off. This call still works then. It returns the whole updated list, like
`GET api/2.0/settings/notification/rooms`.

get.description:
Returns the channels this installation can use to deliver notifications, each with `isEnabled`. The channel
names are `email.sender` for letters and `telegram.sender` for Telegram messages. The list describes the
installation and the portal, so every user gets the same answer. Any signed-in user can call it, including a
guest. The call is read-only. A channel appears only if the notification service configures a sender with that
name. An empty list means the configuration names no channel this build supports. The call always reports
`email.sender` as enabled when it is listed. It reports `telegram.sender` as enabled only while the portal
stores a Telegram bot name and token. To store them, use `POST api/2.0/settings/authservice`. An enabled
channel says nothing about the caller. To get Telegram messages, a user also connects their own Telegram
account. To get the link, use `GET api/2.0/settings/telegram/link`. To check the result, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/telegram/check`. To read which kinds of notification a user receives, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/notification/{type}`.

200.description: The notification channels this installation can deliver through, each with the flag that says whether it is enabled

post.description:
Starts moving the portal to another owner. The portal sends a confirmation letter to the portal owner's email
address. Ownership moves only after `PUT api/2.0/settings/owner` with the link from this letter. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace
admin who is not the portal owner gets 200 with `status` 0 and a refusal text. The call also returns `status` 0
for an unknown or inactive new owner. So read `status`, not the HTTP code. On success, `status` is 1. The
`message` then shows the owner's address as an HTML `mailto:` link. Do not repeat the call. Each successful call
sends a new letter with a new link. Earlier links keep working until ownership moves. A link works for seven days
by default. The call returns 400 if `ownerId` is missing or the owner's email address is not confirmed. To check
the address, read `activationStatus` from `GET api/2.0/people/@self`. It also returns 403 if the new owner is a
guest. To change a user type instead, use `PUT api/2.0/people/type/{type}`.

schema.description: The portal member named as the new owner of the portal.

200.description: The outcome of the request: `status` 1 with the address the instructions were sent to, or `status` 0 with a localized refusal when the transfer cannot be started

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `ownerId`, or the portal owner's own email address has not been confirmed yet, so no instructions can be sent

403.description: The caller does not hold the portal-settings right of a DocSpace administrator, or the user named as the new owner is a guest

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Completes the portal owner change that `POST api/2.0/settings/owner` started. The user in `ownerId` becomes the
portal owner. Sign the request with the confirmation link from that letter, not with a session. A signed-in
caller without this link gets 403, even the portal owner. A caller with neither a session nor this link gets
401. Pass the link's `type`, `key`, `uid`, and `encemail` parameters in the `confirm` header. An invalid or
expired link returns 401. A link expires after seven days by default. It also becomes invalid when its address
no longer belongs to the portal owner. A deleted or disabled `uid` account has the same effect. To check that
the link still works, use `POST api/2.0/authentication/confirm`. The call changes data, and a repeated call
with the same link returns 401. If the new owner is not a DocSpace admin yet, the call makes them one first.
The previous owner keeps their account and role but loses the owner's rights. The call returns no body. To read
the new `ownerId`, use `GET api/2.0/settings` as a signed-in user. After this call, a new transfer needs the
new owner. The new owner must be an active account of the portal, not a guest. If promoting the new owner
needs a paid seat that the portal lacks, the call returns 402. Then ownership does not move. Without `ownerId`,
the call returns 400.

schema.description: The portal member named as the new owner of the portal.

200.description: The portal owner has been changed to the user named in the request

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `ownerId`

401.description: The caller is not signed in and sent no owner change link, or the link is invalid or expired, its address no longer belongs to the portal owner, or its `uid` account is deleted or disabled

402.description: The user named as the new owner is a regular user, and promoting them to DocSpace administrator needs a paid seat the portal has run out of

403.description: The caller is signed in but sent no owner change link, whatever their role, or sent a valid confirmation link of another type

Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call is read-only. If `enableQuota` is false, the portal does not apply the default size. It supports
`If-Modified-Since` with the `Last-Modified` value of the last answer. If nothing changed, it returns 304 with
an empty body.

EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the

post.description:
Replaces logo images of the current portal. The portal shows them on the login page, in the menu, in editors,
and in letters. Each `logo` entry names a slot by its `type` number from
`GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos`. A slot left out of the request keeps its image. Only slots 1, 2, 6,
7, and 8 have a dark image. For other slots, the call ignores `dark`. Saving slot 2 also rebuilds the
notification logo, slot 8, from the light image. The call reads only `logo` from the body. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the
plan has no customization or the installation hides branding, the call returns 402. To check this first, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/enablewhitelabel`. The call changes data and returns `true`. You can repeat it with
base64 images. The call deletes a used temporary file, so a repeat must send that image again. To undo the
call, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/restore`. With `isDefault=true`, the call changes the
installation-wide default logos instead. Only a self-hosted installation without limited space access allows
this. Elsewhere the call returns 403. The call also returns 400 if `logoText` is too long, although it does
not store the text. To upload image files, use `POST api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/savefromfiles`.

post.description:
Replaces logo images of the current portal with files from a `multipart/form-data` request. The call ignores
form field names and reads each file name instead. A file name starts with the slot `type` number from
`GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos`. It ends with the image extension, as in `2.png`. A name that contains
`dark`, as in `2.dark.png`, sets the dark image of the slot. Only slots 1, 2, 6, 7, and 8 have a dark image.
For other slots, the call skips dark files. Slots without a file keep their image. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. A
request without files also returns 403. If the plan has no customization or the installation hides branding,
the call returns 402. The call changes data and returns `true`. You can repeat it with the same files. To undo
the call, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/restore`. With `isDefault=true`, the call changes the
installation-wide default logos instead. Only a self-hosted installation without limited space access allows
this. Elsewhere the call returns 403. To send images as base64, use
`POST api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/save`.

Returns the logo slots of the current portal with the image URLs to show. Anyone can call it without signing
in. The call takes the portal from the request address. The call is read-only. Each item has the slot number
in `type`, its name, its image size, and the URLs in `path`. If `isDark` is `true`, the call fills only
`dark`. If `isDark` is `false`, it fills only `light`. Without `isDark`, the call fills both URLs. Then `dark`
is empty for a slot without a separate dark image. The list leaves out the notification slot 8, which only
letters use. With `isDefault=true`, the call returns the installation-wide default logos instead. To learn
which slots still have built-in images, use `GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/isdefault`.
