EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. Unlike
the save calls, it works without a plan that includes customization. The call deletes the stored image files,
so it cannot be undone. To get the images back, upload them again with
`POST api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/save`. You can repeat the call, and it returns `true` each time. It
resets all slots together, not one by one. For a portal, it also resets the logo of older letter templates. It
does not change the logo text. To reset the text, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logotext/restore`. With
`isDefault=true`, the call resets the installation-wide default logos instead. Only a self-hosted installation
without limited space access allows this. Elsewhere the call returns 403.

page, in editors, and in letters. The call reads only `logoText` from the body. An empty or blank text, or

with the same body. It does not change logo images and does not draw the text into them. With
`isDefault=true`, the call changes the installation-wide default text instead. Only a self-hosted installation
without limited space access allows this. Elsewhere the call returns 403. If the text is too long, the call
returns 400. To read the text, use `GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logotext`.

Changes the company details that the About page and letters show as the vendor. The `settings` object replaces
the whole set, so send every field. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and
DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. Only a self-hosted installation without limited space access

installation hides branding, the call returns 402. The details apply to the whole installation and reach all
its portals. The call always stores `isLicensor` as `false`. It stores `hideAbout` only if the plan includes
branding. The call changes data and returns `true`. You can repeat it with the same body. To undo the call,
use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/rebranding/company`. The call returns 400 if `settings`, `email`, or `site` is
missing or not valid.

get.description:
Returns the access rules of portal modules, one entry per GUID in `ids`. Entries follow the order of `ids`. Each
entry says whether the module is enabled and which groups and users may open it. Without `ids`, the call reports
every module the portal registers. DocSpace registers none, so the list is then empty. Any signed-in user can call
it. The call is read-only. If an `ids` value is not a GUID, the call returns 400. A module that nobody configured
has `enabled` set to `false`. The `users` list leaves out users the caller cannot see. So two callers can get
different lists for one module. The `isSubItem` flag is `true` for a module nested under another module. To change
the rules, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/security`.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
The modules to report on, each given as a GUID and sent as a repeated query value. An entry that is not a
GUID fails the whole request as invalid. Leaving the list out asks about every module registered in the
portal, which on a DocSpace installation is none, so the answer is then empty rather than complete.

200.description: The access configuration of every module identifier asked about: the enabled flag, the allowed groups, the allowed users the caller may see, and the sub-module flag

400.description: An `ids` value is not a GUID

put.description:
Replaces the access rule of one portal module. The rule says whether the module may be opened, and for which users
and groups. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other
callers get 403. The call also returns 403 on an open portal, where everyone is admitted. The call changes data,
and you can repeat it with the same body. It deletes the stored subjects instead of adding to them. So send the
full list of subjects every time. If `subjects` is left out, `enabled` applies to everyone. An empty `subjects`
array gives access to everyone, whatever `enabled` says. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read, has no
`id`, or `id` is not a GUID. It returns the resulting rule as a list with one entry, in the shape of
`GET api/2.0/settings/security`. To switch several modules in one call, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/security/access`.

schema.description: The access rule stored for one portal module: whether it may be opened, and by whom.

200.description: The resulting access configuration of the module, as a single-entry list

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `id`, or the `id` is not a GUID

403.description: Per-module access cannot be configured on an open portal, or the caller lacks the portal-settings right of a DocSpace administrator

get.description:
Returns whether the calling user can open the portal module with the GUID `id`. The answer is a single boolean.
Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only, and the answer depends on the caller. The value `true`
means the module is registered and visible, and the caller may read it. The value `false` covers all other cases:
an unknown module, a hidden module, or a caller outside the allow-list. So `false` does not tell these cases
apart, and an unknown `id` is not an error. A value that is not a GUID does not match the route. To read the
allow-list, use `GET api/2.0/settings/security`. To list the modules the caller can open, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/modules`. To change access, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/security`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The identifier of the object the operation acts on, as the listing operation of that kind of object reports
it. It has to match the shape the route declares - a GUID where the route is typed as one - since a value of
another shape does not match the route at all and is answered as not found.

200.description: Whether the module is registered, visible and readable by the calling user - false covers a module that is not registered here as well as one the caller may not open

get.description:
Returns the portal modules that the calling user can open now. Each entry has the product class name in `id` and
the display name in `title`. Both values are HTML-encoded. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only
and takes no parameters. The list depends on the caller. It leaves out hidden modules, modules whose access rules
exclude the caller, and nested sub-modules. Entries follow the portal's own module order, not the alphabet. An
empty list means the installation registers no such modules. This is the normal case on DocSpace, not an error.
The `id` values are class names, not module GUIDs. Do not pass them to `GET api/2.0/settings/security/{id}`.

200.description: The portal modules the calling user can open, each with its product class name and its display name, in the portal's own module order

get.description:
Returns the password policy of the portal. It has the minimum length and the flags that require an uppercase
letter, a digit, and a special symbol. It also has regular expressions to check a password before sending it. Any
signed-in user can call it. A request signed with the confirmation token from an emailed link also works. So an
invited user or a user who resets a password can check the new password. The call works even if the portal payment
is overdue. The call is read-only. It supports `If-Modified-Since` with the `Last-Modified` value of an earlier
answer. If the policy has not changed since then, the call returns 304 with an empty body. A portal that nobody
configured requires 8 characters with all three flags off. The portal also refuses passwords over 30 characters,
and the answer does not show this limit. To change the policy, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/security/password`.

200.description: The portal password policy: the minimum length, the uppercase, digit and special-symbol requirements, and the regular expressions a client can validate against

304.description: The password policy has not changed since the `Last-Modified` value sent back in `If-Modified-Since`; the body is empty

put.description:
Updates the password policy of the portal with `minLength`, `upperCase`, `digits`, and `specSymbols`. The call
replaces all four values, and a flag left out of the body is stored as `false`. So first read the policy with
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/password`. Then send it back with your change. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you
can repeat it with the same body. The new policy applies only to passwords set after this call. Existing passwords
keep working, and nobody is asked to change them. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read, `minLength` is
missing, or `minLength` is out of range. It returns the stored policy with its regular expressions.

schema.description: The four values that make up the portal password policy, replaced together.

put.summary: Set access to modules in bulk
put.description:
Turns several portal modules on or off in one call. Each `items` entry has a module GUID in `key` and the enabled
flag in `value`. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 on an open portal, where everyone is admitted. The call changes
data, and you can repeat it with the same body. If a module is listed twice, the call applies only its first
entry. The body has no list of users and groups. Turning a product module on restores its last list of users and
groups. In all other cases, the call allows or denies the module for everyone. To change that list, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/security`. If the body cannot be read or a `key` is not a GUID, the call returns 400. It
returns the resulting rules of the listed modules in the shape of `GET api/2.0/settings/security`.

get.description:
Returns the users who administer the portal module with the GUID `productId`. The all-zero GUID means the whole
portal. Then the list covers the DocSpace admin group and every product group, and it includes the portal owner.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call is read-only. If `productId` names no group, the call returns an empty list. Entries come in
group order, with the DocSpace admin group first. A user who is in several of these groups appears once per group.
The list has no paging and no filter. To check one user against one module, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/administrator`. To add or remove an administrator, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/security/administrator`.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description:
The module the operation acts on, by module GUID. The all-zero GUID stands for the portal itself rather than
for a single module, and a GUID that names no module group is answered with an empty result instead of a
failure.

get.description:
Returns whether one user administers one portal module. The answer repeats `productId` and `userId` and adds the
`administrator` flag. The all-zero `productId` asks about the whole portal. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call is read-only. The
flag is `true` if the user is in the DocSpace admin group or in the module group. So a DocSpace admin is an
administrator of every module. Unknown user or module IDs give `false`, not an error. So `false` does not prove
that the user exists. The flag comes only from group membership and does not show whether the module is available.
To check that, use `GET api/2.0/settings/security/{id}`. To list all administrators of a module, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/administrator/{productId}`. To change the role, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/security/administrator`.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description:
The module being asked about, by module GUID. The all-zero GUID asks about the portal itself rather than a
single module.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The account being asked about, by portal user ID. An ID that names no account is answered as a plain negative
rather than a failure, so a negative answer does not prove the account exists.

200.description: The module and the user asked about together with the flag that says whether that user administers the module

put.description:
Adds a portal member to the administrators of one module, or removes the member, by the `administrator` flag. The
all-zero `productId` means the DocSpace admin role for the whole portal. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. Only the portal owner can
grant the DocSpace admin role or take any role away from a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403 for these
changes. On a free cloud plan, the call returns 402. Promoting a guest or a user takes a paid seat. If no paid
seat is left, the call returns 402. Removing the DocSpace admin role also removes the member from every product
group. The call changes data immediately, and you can repeat it with the same body. It never creates a user, so
invite the member first. If the body cannot be read or has no `productId` or `userId`, the call returns 400. The
call returns the identifiers and the flag as sent. To check membership, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/security/administrator`.

get.description:
Returns the SAML single sign-on (SSO) configuration of the portal. Anyone can call it without signing in.
An anonymous caller gets only `hideAuthPage`, and every other field is empty. This flag says if the sign-in
page hides the built-in login form. It is false if a cloud plan lacks SSO or SSO settings are hidden. A
signed-in caller gets the full configuration and needs the EditPortalSettings permission. The portal owner
and DocSpace admins have it. Other signed-in callers get 403. If a cloud plan lacks SSO or SSO settings are
hidden, the call returns 402 to a signed-in caller. The call is read-only. An empty
login label comes back as `Single Sign-on`. A null `enableSso` means that SSO is off. For a blank
configuration, use `GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/default`. For the values that the SAML fields accept, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/constants`.

200.description: The current portal SSO settings; an anonymous caller gets only the hidden-login-form flag

402.description: The caller is signed in, the portal is a cloud one, and its pricing plan has no single sign-on option or the SSO section is not enabled for it

403.description: The caller is signed in and has no portal-settings right

post.description:
Replaces the SAML SSO configuration of the portal with the JSON object in `serializeSettings`. It returns the
saved configuration. The object is a full configuration, not a patch. Left-out fields become empty. Start from
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2` or `GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/default`. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If a cloud plan lacks SSO
or SSO settings are hidden, the call returns 402. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same
body. It changes a `usersType` other than room admin (1), DocSpace admin (3), or user (4) to 4. It saves an
empty login label as `Single Sign-on` and cuts a longer one to 100 characters. If `enableSso` is false or
missing, the call unlinks every SSO account from the identity provider. These accounts become ordinary portal
accounts. Turning SSO back on does not link them again. The call returns 400 if `serializeSettings` is empty,
the JSON `null`, or not valid JSON. A value of the wrong type also returns 400. It also returns 400 if the
JSON lacks `idpSettings` or `fieldMapping`. An empty entity ID, sign-in URL, first name, last name, or email
mapping also returns 400. A sign-in or sign-out URL that is not an absolute http or https address also returns
400. Then the call saves nothing. For the values of the SAML fields, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/constants`.

schema.description: The whole SAML Single Sign-On configuration of the portal, carried as a serialised JSON object.

200.description: The SSO settings as they were stored, with the login label and the user type normalised

400.description: The serialized settings are empty, not valid JSON, have a value of the wrong type or do not contain an SSO configuration object, the `idpSettings` object is missing or its entity ID is empty, the SSO URL is missing or the SSO or SLO URL is not an absolute HTTP or HTTPS address, or the `fieldMapping` object is missing or its first name, last name or email attribute is empty

delete.description:
Deletes the SAML SSO configuration of the portal and saves the built-in default one instead. It returns the
saved configuration, which matches `GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/default`. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the plan of a cloud
portal does not include SSO or SSO settings are hidden, the call returns 402. The call cannot be undone, and
you can repeat it. It turns SSO off and deletes the identity provider addresses, certificates, attribute
mapping, and login label. It also unlinks every SSO account from the identity provider. These accounts
become ordinary portal accounts and keep their data and contacts. To keep a copy, first save the result of
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2`. To turn SSO off and keep the configuration, set `enableSso` to false in
`POST api/2.0/settings/ssov2`.

200.description: The default SSO configuration that is now in effect

get.description:
Returns the built-in SSO configuration that a portal starts from. It has empty identity provider fields,
the usual SAML values, and SSO turned off. The values are the same for every portal and do not depend on the
saved configuration. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins
have. Other callers get 403. If the plan of a cloud portal does not include SSO or SSO settings are hidden,
the call returns 402. The call is read-only. To create a configuration, fill in the identity provider entity
ID, sign-in URL, and certificates of the result. Then send it to `POST api/2.0/settings/ssov2`. To reset the
saved configuration to these values, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/ssov2`.

200.description: The built-in SSO configuration a portal starts from

402.description: The portal is a cloud one, and its pricing plan has no single sign-on option or the SSO section is not enabled for it

get.description:
Returns every value that the SAML fields of the SSO configuration accept, grouped by field. The groups are
name ID formats, bindings, signing and encryption algorithms, and certificate uses. Any signed-in user can
call it. The call is read-only. The values are SAML URNs and algorithm URIs, so copy them into the
configuration as they are. The save call `POST api/2.0/settings/ssov2` stores these fields without checks.
So a misspelled value fails only later, at sign-in. The list is the same for every portal and changes only
with a new release, so you can cache it. For a configuration with the usual values, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/default`.

200.description: Every value the SAML fields accept: name ID formats, bindings, signing and encryption algorithms, and the service provider and identity provider certificate uses

get.description:
Returns the storage space that one module of the portal uses, per category of its data. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only. It returns the whole list without paging. Sizes are display texts, such as `1.5 GB`, not
byte counts. If no module has this `id`, or the module does not count space, the call returns an empty list.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The identifier of the object the operation acts on, as the listing operation of that kind of object reports
it. It has to match the shape the route declares - a GUID where the route is typed as one - since a value of
another shape does not match the route at all and is answered as not found.

get.description:
Returns the third-party storages that can keep the portal data, such as Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage. The
built-in local storage is not in the list. If no entry is `current`, the portal keeps its data in the local
storage. Each entry shows its keys and whether the server has them set (`isSet`). Keys of the current storage
come from the saved settings. Keys of other storages come from the provider configuration and are empty if
nobody set them. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access
space. The call is read-only. To switch the storage, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage`. To return to the local
storage, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage`. For the CDN and backup storages, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn` and `GET api/2.0/settings/storage/backup`.

200.description: The storages available to the portal, each marked as configured and as currently in use

403.description: The caller may not edit portal settings, or this installation does not allow changing the storage

put.description:
Switches the portal to another storage and starts moving the portal data to it. Set `module` to an entry of
`GET api/2.0/settings/storage` and `props` to the keys of that provider. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if
the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access space. The call queues work. The portal stays
unavailable until the move ends. Repeat `GET api/2.0/settings/storage/progress` until it returns 100. Do not
send another switch during a move. If `module` is already the current storage, the call changes nothing and
returns the current settings. Otherwise, it returns the requested settings, not the state of the move. If the
provider of `module` is not set on the server (`isSet` is false), the call returns 400. To return to the local
storage, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage`. To select a CDN, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`.

delete.description:
Clears the third-party storage of the portal and starts moving the portal data back to the local storage.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access space. The call
queues work and returns no body. The portal stays unavailable until the move ends. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/settings/storage/progress` until it returns 100. You can repeat the call. During a move, a
repeated call starts no second move. The move copies the documents and does not delete them. The call deletes
the saved keys of the previous storage. To switch back, send them again with `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage`.
Before `POST api/2.0/settings/encryption/start`, reset the storage with this call.

200.description: The storage configuration has been cleared and migration back to the local storage has started

get.description:
Returns the progress of moving the portal data to another storage, as a percentage from 0 to 100. To start the
move, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage` or `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage`. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call works even if the
portal is not paid. The call is read-only. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until the value reaches 100. Then
the portal works from the new storage. If the server has no migration for the portal, the call fails with a
server error. On an installation that is not self-hosted, the call returns -1. The value does not show migration
errors. If it stops growing, check the portal state with `GET api/2.0/portal`.

200.description: Migration progress as a percentage, or -1 where storage migration is not offered

get.description:
Returns the storages that can serve the static content of the portal through a CDN. The list has only the
providers of `GET api/2.0/settings/storage` that offer a CDN. Each entry shows its keys, whether the server has
them set (`isSet`), and whether the portal uses it (`current`). Keys of the current entry come from the saved
CDN settings. If no entry is `current`, the portal serves its static content itself. An empty list means that
the build has no CDN provider. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace
admins have. Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits
the access space. The call is read-only. To select a CDN, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`. To stop using
one, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`.

200.description: The storages that can serve as the portal CDN, with the one in use marked as current

put.description:
Selects the CDN that serves the static content of the portal and starts copying the content to it. Set `module`
to an entry of `GET api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn` and `props` to the keys of that provider. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call
also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access space. The call queues work. No
call shows its progress. The content appears on the CDN after the server copies it. You can repeat it. If
`module` is already the current CDN, the call changes nothing and returns the current settings. Otherwise, it
returns the requested CDN settings. If the provider of `module` is not set on the server (`isSet` is false), the
call returns 400. The call does not move documents. To move them, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage`.

delete.description:
Clears the CDN settings of the portal, so the portal serves its static content itself again. The call does not
upload, move, or delete files. Files on the CDN stay there until you delete them in the provider console. Links
that the portal builds after the call no longer use the CDN. An open page may use the CDN until you reload it.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. The call also returns 403 if the installation is not self-hosted or limits the access space. The call
changes data and returns no body. You can repeat it. To see the current CDN, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`. To select a CDN again, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`. To reset the
document storage, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/storage`.

200.description: The CDN configuration has been cleared and static content is served by the portal again

get.description:
Returns the storages that can keep portal backups. The storage of the saved backup schedule is `current`, with
its keys from the schedule. If no schedule exists or it uses no third-party storage, no entry is `current`.
Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers
get 403. If the installation is not self-hosted and offers no backup, the call also returns 403. The call is
read-only. It does not show where the portal keeps its data. To change that storage, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/storage`.

which schedule marks an entry as `current`; the list of storages itself is the same either way, and the flag
makes sense only on a self-hosted installation.

get.description:
Returns the Amazon regions that the server knows, with their display names and partition details. The list is
built into the server, so it is the same for every portal. It changes only with a server update, so you can
cache it. Use the system name of an entry as the region in `props` of an Amazon S3 storage. This applies to
`PUT api/2.0/settings/storage`, `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage/cdn`, and a backup schedule. Pick the region from
this list. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The list has no paging or filters.

200.description: The Amazon regions known to this installation

get.description:
Returns whether the current user's account is linked to the portal's Telegram bot. Linking needs a bot that
`POST api/2.0/settings/authservice` configures for the portal. Any signed-in user can call it, including a
guest. The call is read-only and covers only the caller's own account. The `status` field is `unlinked`,
`linked`, or `linking`. The value `linking` means the user got a registration link but has not opened it in
Telegram yet. This state ends when the user opens the link or the link expires. The `username` field is
filled only when `status` is `linked`. To start linking, use `GET api/2.0/settings/telegram/link`. To remove
a link, use `DELETE api/2.0/settings/telegram/link`.

200.description: The current user's Telegram link state, with the username filled in only when linked

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the personal `t.me` link that connects the current user's account to the portal's Telegram bot. After
linking, the portal can send the user notifications in Telegram. Linking needs a bot that
`POST api/2.0/settings/authservice` configures for the portal. Without a bot name, the call returns an empty
link. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest. The call changes data. If the user has no valid registration token, it issues a new one. A repeated call
returns the same link while the token is valid. The token expires in 20 minutes by default. After that, call
this operation again for a new link. The user completes linking by opening the link in Telegram. Then poll
`GET api/2.0/settings/telegram/check` until `status` is `linked`. To remove a link, use
`DELETE api/2.0/settings/telegram/link`.

200.description: A `t.me` deep link that connects the caller's account to the portal's Telegram bot

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

delete.description:
Deletes the link between the current user's account and the portal's Telegram bot. After this call, the
portal no longer sends the user notifications in Telegram. Any signed-in user can call it, including a guest.
The call deletes only the caller's own link, and other members keep theirs. The call changes data, and you can
repeat it. It returns `true` both when it deleted a link and when there was none. The chat stays in the user's
Telegram. The bot settings of the portal and the other notification channels do not change. To list the channels of the portal, use `GET api/2.0/settings/notification/channels`. To link the
account again, use `GET api/2.0/settings/telegram/link`.

200.description: Always `true` once the caller has no link to the Telegram bot

get.description:
Returns the two-factor authentication methods the portal offers, with the portal-wide state of each. The list
has at most two entries, `sms` and `app`. Each entry appears only if the installation offers its method. Its
`available` field says if the portal can turn it on. An empty list means the portal offers neither method. Any
signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. It returns the portal policy, not the caller's own linked
app. To change the policy, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaapp`. To read your own backup codes, use `GET
api/2.0/settings/tfaappcodes`.

200.description: The TFA methods the portal offers, with the portal-wide state of each

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Sets the portal-wide two-factor authentication policy. With `type` `1`, it switches on the SMS method, and with
`2`, the authenticator app. Any other `type`, including `0`, turns TFA off. Switching one method on switches the
other off. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other
callers get 403. If `id` or `mandatoryUsers` names the portal owner while `id` is not the caller, the call
returns 403. The call changes data and replaces the trusted and mandatory lists. Switching a method on signs out
every session on the portal, including the caller's. With `type` `1` or `2`, a repeated call saves the same
policy and signs everyone out again. You can repeat a call that turns TFA off. It returns `true` if it switched
a method on. It returns `false` if it turned TFA off. To also get the caller's own confirmation link, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaappwithlink`. If the method is unavailable on the portal or SMS has no provider, the
call returns 405. The call returns 400 for an unreadable `type` or a malformed ID. It also returns 400 if a
`trustedIps` entry is not an address, range, or CIDR block. It works even when the portal payment is overdue.

schema.description: The portal two-factor policy: which method is in force, who must pass it, and from where it is waived.

200.description: `true` when the SMS or the authenticator method was switched on, `false` when TFA was turned off

400.description: The request body cannot be read, `type` is `null`, an empty string or a string that is neither a number nor built from the names `None`, `Sms` and `App`, or a `trustedIps` entry is not a single address, an inclusive range or a CIDR block

403.description: The caller has no portal-settings right, or names the owner's account in `id` or `mandatoryUsers` while `id` is not the caller's own

405.description: The requested method is not enabled on this portal, or the SMS method has no configured provider

post.description:
Checks a two-factor code for the account of the confirmation link. Then it completes the pending TFA step. Sign
the request with the confirmation token of a `TfaActivation` or `TfaAuth` link. The sign-in flow or
`GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/confirm` issues that link. With an ordinary sign-in token, the call returns 403. It
accepts a code from the app or an unused backup code, which it spends. The call changes data and signs the
account in. It clears the confirmation cookie, but the key stays valid for one hour by default. A repeat with
that key accepts the same app code for 5 minutes. It signs in again and returns `false`. For a `TfaAuth` link,
send the repeat without the new session cookie. A repeat with a spent backup code returns 400. On the first
activation, it also generates the backup codes. It returns `true` for the first activation, and `false` if an
app was already linked. If the authenticator method is off on the portal, the call checks no code and returns
`false`. If the code is wrong, the call returns 400. If the account exceeds the portal login attempt limit
within a minute, the call returns 403. The call works even when the portal payment is overdue.

schema.description: The one-time code that completes a pending two-factor step, and how long the resulting sign-in lasts.

200.description: `true` when the code completed a first activation and backup codes were generated, `false` when an application was already linked

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `code`, or the code matches neither the authenticator application nor an unused backup code

403.description: The account the confirmation link was issued for has used up the portal's login attempt limit for TFA codes

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the confirmation link that the current user follows to pass the portal two-factor step. Any signed-in
user can call it, always for their own account. If the portal policy does not require TFA from the caller, the
response body is empty. With the SMS method, the call is read-only and fills only `url`. The link activates a
phone while the account has no activated number. After that, it authorizes the phone. With the authenticator
method, the call changes data. It issues a new confirmation key and sets it as a cookie. Earlier keys stay valid
for one hour by default. The link activates an app while none is linked. Once one is linked, it verifies a code.
If the portal last turned TFA off and the app was linked over a day ago, the call unlinks it. To send the code
from that flow, use `POST api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/validate`. To read the portal policy, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp`.

200.description: The confirmation link for the caller's TFA step, with the cookie filled in for the authenticator method

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.summary: Update TFA settings with a link
put.description:
Sets the portal-wide two-factor policy as `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaapp` does. It also returns the caller's own
confirmation link. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have.
Other callers get 403. If `id` or `mandatoryUsers` names the portal owner while `id` is not the caller, the call
returns 403. Any `type` other than `1` and `2` turns TFA off. The call changes data. Switching a method on signs
out every session on the portal. With `type` `1` or `2`, a repeated call signs everyone out again and returns a
new link. You can repeat a call that turns TFA off. The call returns an empty string if it turned TFA off or the
caller is exempt. Usually, the caller is exempt through their own address in `trustedIps`. For the authenticator
method, the call sets the link's cookie but does not return its value. To get the value, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/confirm`, which issues a new link. If the method is unavailable on the portal or
SMS has no provider, the call returns 405. The call returns 400 for an unreadable `type` or a malformed ID. It
also returns 400 if a `trustedIps` entry is not an address, range, or CIDR block.

schema.description: The portal two-factor policy: which method is in force, who must pass it, and from where it is waived.

200.description: The caller's own confirmation link, or an empty string when TFA was turned off or the caller is exempt

400.description: The request body cannot be read, `type` is `null`, an empty string or a string that is neither a number nor built from the names `None`, `Sms` and `App`, or a `trustedIps` entry is not a single address, an inclusive range or a CIDR block

get.description:
Returns the secret that the current user enters in an authenticator app, as a QR code and a key. Sign the
request with the confirmation token of a `TfaActivation` link. With an ordinary sign-in token, the call returns
403. The sign-in flow or `GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/confirm` issues that link. The
authenticator method must be the current portal policy, and the account must have no app linked. Otherwise, the
call returns 405. To replace a linked app, first unlink it with `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaappnewapp`. The first
call changes data and creates the secret. Later calls return the same secret until the app is unlinked. To
finish the setup, send a code from the app to `POST api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/validate`. The call works even when
the portal payment is overdue.

200.description: The account label, the manual entry key and the QR-code image for linking an authenticator application

403.description: The request is signed with an ordinary sign-in token, not with the confirmation token of a TfaActivation link

405.description: The authenticator method is not enabled on this portal, or the account already has an application linked

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the backup codes of the current user's authenticator app, including the spent ones. At sign-in, each
backup code can replace a code from the app once. Any signed-in user can call it, always for their own account.
There is no way to read the codes of another account. If the authenticator method is unavailable or off on the
portal, or no app is linked, the call returns 405. To link an app, use `GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/confirm` and
then `POST api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/validate`. The call is read-only. The portal generates the codes when the app
is first linked. To replace the whole set, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaappnewcodes`. By default, there are five
codes of six characters. The installation can set another number and length.

200.description: The caller's backup codes, each with the flag showing whether it has already been used

405.description: The authenticator method is not enabled on this portal, or the caller has no application linked

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Replaces the current user's backup codes with a new set and returns it. Use it after the old codes are spent or
may have leaked. Any signed-in user can call it, always for their own account. If the authenticator method is
unavailable on the portal or no app is linked, the call returns 405. The call changes data, and the old codes
stop working immediately. Store the new codes before you leave the response. Do not repeat it. Each call creates
another set and discards the previous one, so a retry returns different codes. The new codes are unused. By
default, there are five codes of six characters. The installation can set another number and length. The secret
of the linked app does not change, so the app keeps working. To read the current set without a change, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/tfaappcodes`.

200.description: The newly generated backup codes, all unused, replacing the caller's previous set

405.description: The authenticator method is not enabled on this portal, or the caller has no application linked

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Unlinks the authenticator app from an account. While the portal requires TFA, the account must link a new app at
its next sign-in. To reset your own app, pass your own ID in `id`. Only the portal owner can reset the app of
another account. Other callers get 403, including DocSpace admins. The call also returns 403 for a missing or
unknown `id`, the empty GUID, or a terminated account. If the authenticator method is unavailable on the portal
or the account has no app linked, the call returns 405. The call changes data and cannot be undone. It deletes
the app and the backup codes of the account. It also signs out all sessions of the account. For your own
account, it then sets a new session cookie. A repeated call returns 405. For your own account, the call returns
the activation link to follow next and sets its confirmation cookie. For another account, the call returns an
empty string and emails its user about the reset. The portal policy does not change. The account links a new app
through `GET api/2.0/settings/tfaapp/confirm`. To turn TFA off for everyone, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaapp`.
The call returns 400 if a body field is unreadable, such as an `id` that is not a GUID.

schema.description: The portal two-factor policy: which method is in force, who must pass it, and from where it is waived.

200.description: The activation link when the caller reset their own application, or an empty string when another member's was reset

400.description: The request body cannot be read, `type` is `null`, an empty string or a string that is neither a number nor built from the names `None`, `Sms` and `App`, or a `trustedIps` entry is not a single address, an inclusive range or a CIDR block, although this call reads only `id`

403.description: The caller is not the portal owner, the account cannot be resolved from `id`, or the account is terminated

405.description: The authenticator method is not enabled on this portal, or the account has no application linked

get.description:
Returns the webhook subscriptions of the portal, each with the outcome of its last delivery. Any signed-in
user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. If the portal restricts the developer tools, only DocSpace
admins can call it. Other callers then get 403. To read this setting, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/devtoolsaccess`. The portal owner and DocSpace admins see every subscription. Other
users see only the subscriptions they created. The call is read-only. The response never contains the secret
key. The list has no paging and no fixed order. An empty list means that the caller has no subscriptions. To
create a subscription, use `POST api/2.0/settings/webhook`. To read single deliveries, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/webhooks/log`.

200.description: The webhook subscriptions visible to the caller, each with the status of its last delivery

403.description: The caller is a `Guest`, or a non-admin caller while the developer tools are restricted

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Creates a webhook subscription of the portal. The portal then posts a signed JSON payload to `uri` when a
subscribed event happens. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. If the portal
restricts the developer tools, only DocSpace admins can call it. Other callers then get 403. The call changes
data. A repeated call with the same `name` and `uri` returns 400. The response never contains the secret key.
Before saving, the call sends a HEAD request to `uri` and does not follow redirects. If you leave out `ssl`, it
is `true` for an `https` address and `false` for an `http` one. If `triggers` is 0, the subscription gets every
event that the role of its creator allows. To find the triggers your role allows, use
`GET api/2.0/settings/webhook/triggers`. A subscription delivers only while it is on, and only events that its
creator can see. The call returns 400 if `name` or `uri` is empty, a value is too long, or `uri` is not allowed.
It also returns 400 if `uri` answers the HEAD request with an error code. It also returns 400 if `secretKey`
breaks the password rules or your role does not allow a trigger. For user or group events, `targetId` must name
a user or group that you can see. If it does not, the call returns 400.

put.description:
Changes all parameters of a webhook subscription that the body names by `id`. The call overwrites every stored
field with the body. So a left-out `enabled`, `triggers`, or `targetId` becomes `false`, 0, or empty. First
read the current values with `GET api/2.0/settings/webhook`. Then send back the values that must stay. Two
fields are exceptions. An empty `secretKey` keeps the stored secret. A left-out `ssl` keeps the stored
setting. So pass `ssl` when you move the target between `http` and `https`. Any signed-in user can call it,
except a guest. A guest gets 403. The portal owner and DocSpace admins can change any subscription. Other
users can change only the subscriptions they created and get 403 for others. If the portal restricts the
developer tools, users who are not DocSpace admins get 403 too. The call changes data. You can repeat it with
the same body. A missing `name` or `uri` returns 400 before any other check. If no subscription has this `id`,
the call returns 404 before the access check. Then the call checks the body as `POST api/2.0/settings/webhook`
does. It checks the triggers against the role of the subscription's creator, not of the caller. If a check
fails, the call returns 400. To turn a subscription on or off only, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook/enable`.

200.description: The updated webhook subscription, without its secret key

put.summary: Switch a webhook on or off
put.description:
Turns a webhook subscription on or off and keeps its other parameters. The call reads only `id` and `enabled`
from the body. The schema still requires `name` and `uri`, but the call ignores their values. To change other
fields, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook`. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403.
The portal owner and DocSpace admins can switch any subscription. Other users can switch only the
subscriptions they created and get 403 for others. If the portal restricts the developer tools, users who are
not DocSpace admins get 403 too. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body. If no
subscription has this `id`, the call returns 404 before the access check. Turning a subscription off checks
nothing. Turning it on checks the stored values again. The call sends a HEAD request to the stored address. It
checks the stored secret against the current password rules. It checks the stored triggers against the current
role of the subscription's creator. If any of these checks fails, the call returns 400. So you cannot turn on
a subscription whose target no longer works. Update the subscription first.

delete.description:
Deletes a webhook subscription of the portal by its `id`. The portal then stops queueing its events. Any
signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. The portal owner and DocSpace admins can delete
any subscription. Other users can delete only the subscriptions they created and get 403 for others. If the
portal restricts the developer tools, users who are not DocSpace admins get 403 too. The call cannot be
undone. A repeated call returns 404. The response returns the subscription as it was before the deletion,
without the secret key. To restore a subscription, create it again with `POST api/2.0/settings/webhook`. It
then gets a new `id`, and you must send the secret key again. To pause deliveries and keep the settings, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook/enable`. If no subscription has this `id`, the call returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The identifier of the object the operation acts on, as the listing operation of that kind of object reports
it. It has to match the shape the route declares - a GUID where the route is typed as one - since a value of
another shape does not match the route at all and is answered as not found.

200.description: The removed webhook subscription, as it was just before the removal

get.description:
Returns the delivery log of the portal webhooks, newest first. Each record is one delivery of an event.
Automatic retries update the same record. A manual retry adds a new record with the same `eventId`. Any
signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. If the portal restricts the developer tools,
only DocSpace admins can call it. Other callers then get 403. Users who are not DocSpace admins see only the
deliveries of their own subscriptions. For them, the call replaces `userId` with their own ID. The call is
read-only. The call pages with `startIndex` and `count`, up to 100 records a page. The response gives the
number of matching records in `total`. All filters combine with AND. A `groupStatus` or `trigger` of 0 means
no filter. To get every record of one event, filter by its `eventId`. With the `id` of a manual retry record
as `eventId`, the call returns only that record. If `count` is out of its range, the call returns 400.

parameters.name: deliveryFrom
parameters.description:
The earliest delivery moment a record may carry. Records of attempts still on their way have no delivery
moment yet and fall outside any bound set here.

parameters.name: deliveryTo
parameters.description:
The latest delivery moment a record may carry. All the filters combine with AND, so it narrows whatever the
other ones already kept.

parameters.name: hookUri
parameters.description:
The subscription target address, matched in full rather than as a prefix. Filtering by `configId` is the
reliable way to pick one subscription, since several may share an address.

parameters.name: configId
parameters.description: The subscription whose deliveries are kept, by the `id` that `GET api/2.0/settings/webhook` reports.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: One event, by the `eventId` of its delivery records, which is also the `event.id` the receiver got.

parameters.name: groupStatus
parameters.description: The classes of answered status to keep, as a bitmask; 0 keeps every record whatever the target answered.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The member whose subscriptions the records belong to, by portal user ID - who created the subscription, not
who caused the event. For a caller who is not a DocSpace administrator it is overwritten with the caller own
ID, so such a caller never sees another member deliveries whatever is sent here.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.description:
The single event kind to keep; 0 keeps every kind. It names one trigger rather than a mask of several, unlike
the `triggers` a subscription is created with.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
How many records one page may hold. The maximum is also the default, so a client that wants shorter pages has
to ask for them; the number of records matching the filter comes back as `total` beside the page.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
How many matching records to skip before the page begins, counting from the newest. Advance it by `count` to
walk back through the log.

200.description: The matching delivery records, newest first, with the total count reported beside them

400.description: The `count` is outside its allowed range

403.description: The caller is a `Guest`, or a non-admin caller while the developer tools are restricted

put.description:
Sends one past webhook delivery again. The path `id` is a delivery record from
`GET api/2.0/settings/webhooks/log`, not a subscription. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A
guest gets 403. The portal owner and DocSpace admins can retry any delivery. Other users can retry only
deliveries of their own subscriptions and get 403 for others. If the portal restricts the developer tools,
users who are not DocSpace admins get 403 too. The call queues work. It returns a new delivery record with its
own `id`, the old `eventId`, and the caller in `retriedBy`. The old record keeps its outcome. Each call queues
a new delivery and stops the deliveries queued earlier for the event. The receiver gets the same event ID in a
body that the portal signs again. To learn the outcome, poll `GET api/2.0/settings/webhooks/log` with
`eventId` set to the returned `id`. Repeat it until `nextAttemptOn` is empty. Then a set `delivery` means
success, and an empty one means that the portal gave up. On the default schedule, the portal tries six more
times over about 18 hours. The call is rate limited. More calls return 429. If `id` is 0, the call
returns 400. If no delivery record has this `id`, the call returns 404. It returns 409 and queues nothing for
an event being sent now, a disabled subscription, or an outdated record.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The identifier of the object the operation acts on, as the listing operation of that kind of object reports
it. It has to match the shape the route declares - a GUID where the route is typed as one - since a value of
another shape does not match the route at all and is answered as not found.

200.description: The new delivery record queued for the event, with its own identifier and the retried record's event identifier

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Rate limit: 5 requests per 15 minutes per user/IP.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current 15-minute window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the current 15-minute window resets.

409.description: Nothing was queued: a delivery of the same event is being sent at this moment, the subscription is disabled, or the record predates the current delivery format

put.description:
Sends several past webhook deliveries again. The body lists delivery records from
`GET api/2.0/settings/webhooks/log` in `ids`. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest
gets 403. If the portal restricts the developer tools, only DocSpace admins can call it. Other callers then
get 403. The call queues work. For each record, it queues a new delivery of the same event and returns the new
record. Each new record has its own `id`, the old `eventId`, and the caller in `retriedBy`. Each call also
stops the deliveries queued earlier for these events. The call retries each event once and skips other records
of the same event. It also skips unknown records and records that it cannot queue now. Users who are not
DocSpace admins can retry only records of their own subscriptions. The call skips other records for them. So
compare the response with `ids`. An empty `ids` queues nothing. Each receiver gets the same event ID in a body
that the portal signs again. To learn the outcome, poll `GET api/2.0/settings/webhooks/log` with `eventId` set
to each returned `id`. Repeat it until `nextAttemptOn` is empty. Then a set `delivery` means success, and an
empty one means that the portal gave up. The call is rate limited. More calls return 429. If `ids` has more
than 100 records, the call returns 400. To learn why the call skipped a record, use
`PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook/{id}/retry`.

schema.description: Which past webhook deliveries are sent again.

200.description: The new delivery records, one for every event that could be retried, each with its own identifier

get.description:
Returns the events that a webhook subscription can listen to. Any signed-in user can call it, including a
guest. The developer tools restriction does not apply here. The call is read-only. The list is the same for
every portal and has no paging. It shows user, group, file, folder, room, form, and agent events, in this
order. To build `triggers`, add the `id` values of the wanted events. The entry `*` has the value 0 and means
every event that the role of the creator allows. Use it alone. The `available` field shows whether your role
can subscribe to the event. The list also includes the events that your role cannot use. The portal refuses
such an event when you create or change a subscription.

200.description: The triggers a webhook may subscribe to, each marked available for the caller's role or not

post.description:
Installs a web plugin in the portal from an uploaded package and switches it on. Send the package as
`multipart/form-data`. The archive holds a `config.json` manifest and a `plugin.js` script. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the
installation turns off web plugins or their upload, the call also returns 403. Set `system` to true to
install the plugin for every portal. If the installation is not standalone, `system` set to true returns 403.
The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same package. A package with an installed name replaces its
files, keeps its settings, and switches the plugin on again. The call adds the manifest domains to the portal
Content Security Policy. If this makes the policy header too large, the call returns 403, but the plugin stays
installed. The call returns 400 if the request has no file, several files, or a file that is not a `.zip`. It
also returns 400 for an empty or too large file, or a bad archive or manifest. A manifest name has only
lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.`, and `-`. It also returns 400 if another plugin uses the same JavaScript
object name, `pluginName`. A new plugin also returns 400 if the portal already has the maximum, 100 plugins by
default. To list plugins, use `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins`.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description:
Whether the plugin is installed for every portal of the installation rather than only this one. It is
accepted on a self-hosted installation alone and refused with 403 elsewhere; an installation-wide plugin also
hides a portal plugin that carries the same name.

200.description: The installed web plugin, enabled, with the `url` its script is served from

400.description: The uploaded package is missing, more than one file was sent, the package is of the wrong type, empty or too large, the archive or its manifest is rejected, or the portal already holds the maximum number of plugins

403.description: The caller has no portal-settings right, the request is not a form, web plugins or plugin uploads are switched off for the installation, `system` was requested outside a standalone installation, or the domains the plugin declares would push the Content Security Policy header over its size limit

get.description:
Returns the web plugins of the portal, including the plugins installed for the whole installation. The
installation-wide plugins come first, then the portal plugins. The list does not show a portal plugin with
the name of an installation-wide plugin. Any signed-in user can call it. If the installation turns off web
plugins, the call returns 403. The call is read-only. Each entry includes the `enabled` state and the
`settings` that the portal stored for the plugin. With `enabled` set, the call returns only the plugins in
that state. An empty list means that the portal has no plugins of this kind. The list has no paging and at
most 100 plugins by default. To get one plugin, use `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins/{name}`.

parameters.name: enabled

Which plugins are kept: `true` the ones switched on, `false` the ones switched off. Omitting it lists every
installed plugin whatever its state.

get.summary: Get a web plugin by name
get.description:
Returns one web plugin of the portal by its manifest name. The call searches the same plugins as
`GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins`, including the installation-wide ones. Take the name from the `name` field
of that list. The call ignores the case of the name. Any signed-in user can call it. If the installation
turns off web plugins, the call returns 403. The call is read-only. The response includes the `enabled` state
and the `settings` that the portal stored for the plugin. If no plugin has this name, the call returns 404. To
change the state of the plugin, use `PUT api/2.0/settings/webplugins/{name}`.

The plugin to act on, by the manifest name `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins` publishes as `name`, matched
without regard to case. It is neither the localized display name nor the JavaScript object name in
`pluginName`; a name that is not installed answers 404.

put.description:
Switches an installed web plugin of the portal on or off and saves its settings string. To install a plugin,
use `POST api/2.0/settings/webplugins`. Take the name from the `name` field of
`GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins`. The call ignores the case of the name. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the installation turns
off web plugins, the call also returns 403. The call changes data. The body replaces the stored state and
settings, so you can repeat the call with the same body. Switching the plugin on adds the domains of its
manifest to the portal Content Security Policy. Switching it off removes them. If the domains make the policy
header too large, the call returns 403, but saves the new state. The call returns 400 if the body has no
`settings` or `settings` is too long. If no plugin has this name, the call returns 404.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
The plugin to change, by the manifest name `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins` publishes as `name`, matched
without regard to case. It is neither the localized display name nor the JavaScript object name in
`pluginName`, so it cannot be read off the interface; a name that is not installed answers 404.

requestBody.description:
The whole state the plugin is to have afterwards. It replaces what was stored instead of merging into it, so
both the enabled flag and the settings have to be sent every time.

delete.description:
Deletes a web plugin from the portal together with the files of its package. Take the name from the `name`
field of `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins`. The call ignores the case of the name. Requires the
EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the
installation turns off web plugins or their deletion, the call also returns 403. A plugin with `system` set to
true is installation-wide. Only a standalone installation can delete it. Other installations get 403. Its
deletion removes the plugin from every portal. The call cannot be undone. It deletes the stored state and
settings of the plugin and removes its domains from the portal Content Security Policy. To restore the plugin,
upload its package again with `POST api/2.0/settings/webplugins`. Its old settings do not come back. If no
plugin has this name or its files are missing in storage, the call returns 404. A repeated call returns 404.
To keep the plugin but stop it, switch it off with `PUT api/2.0/settings/webplugins/{name}`.

The plugin to act on, by the manifest name `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins` publishes as `name`, matched
without regard to case. It is neither the localized display name nor the JavaScript object name in
`pluginName`; a name that is not installed answers 404.

put.description:
Reloads a web plugin whose files someone replaced in storage without an upload. For example, a deployment can
put a new version of an installation-wide plugin in storage. Take the name from the `name` field of
`GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins`. The call ignores the case of the name. Requires the EditPortalSettings
permission, which the portal owner and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. If the installation turns
off web plugins, the call also returns 403. The call compares the version it serves with the `version` of the
manifest in storage. The server reloads the plugin list if they differ or the plugin appeared or disappeared.
For an installation-wide plugin, it reloads the list of every portal. The call changes data only then, so you
can repeat it. It does not change the stored state, the settings, or the Content Security Policy. The call
returns the plugin as the portal serves it after the check. If no plugin has this name after the check, the
call returns 404. To install a new version, use `POST api/2.0/settings/webplugins`.

The plugin to act on, by the manifest name `GET api/2.0/settings/webplugins` publishes as `name`, matched
without regard to case. It is neither the localized display name nor the JavaScript object name in
`pluginName`; a name that is not installed answers 404.

get.description:
Returns the OAuth 2.0 consent URL of an external provider as a string. The user opens it in a browser to give
the portal access to their account. First, save the client ID, secret, and redirect URI of the provider with
`POST api/2.0/settings/authservice`. Without them, the URL has no `client_id`, and the provider refuses it.
Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The URL also asks for the scopes the portal needs, such
as Drive with offline access for Google. Its `state` points to the `thirdparty/{provider}/code` page of the
portal. There, the provider returns the code, or an error if the user declines. Only Google, Dropbox,
DocuSign, Box, OneDrive, WordPress, and GitHub produce a URL. For any other provider, the call returns 200
with no URL. If the provider is not a valid value, the call returns 400. With `desktop=true` in the query, the
call copies the query string into `state` for the callback. This call does not exchange the code. To
connect a storage account, pass the code as `token` to `POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty`.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
The provider whose consent screen is wanted. Only Google, Dropbox, Docusign, Box, OneDrive, Wordpress and
Github produce a URL; any other provider is answered with 200 and no URL rather than an error. The provider
credentials have to be saved with `POST api/2.0/settings/authservice` first, or the URL comes back without a
client identifier and the provider refuses it.

200.description: The consent URL of the provider, ready to be opened in a browser; empty when the requested provider is not one of the seven this operation supports

400.description: The `provider` in the path is not one of the login provider names or numbers

loginEvent.description:
The `id` of the item in `items` that the current request is authenticated by. It is `0` when the request

items.description: One open connection of a user: where the sign-in behind it came from, and the ID it can be closed by.

One item per sign-in of the caller that is still active, ordered newest sign-in first, with the connection
the request itself uses moved to the front. Sign-ins older than a year are left out, and a caller with no
stored connection gets a single item describing the current request rather than an empty list.

ActiveConnectionsDto.description: The connections the calling user currently has open, and which of them the request itself was made with.

id.description:
The ID of the sign-in this connection was opened by. Pass it as `loginEventId` to
`PUT api/2.0/security/activeconnections/logout/{loginEventId}` to end this one connection; the item whose
value equals `loginEvent` is the connection the current request uses.

tenantId.description:
The portal the sign-in was made on. The operation never crosses portals, so it is the current one on every
item.

userId.description:
The user the connection belongs to, which is the calling user on every item - the operation cannot report
anyone else's connections.

mobile.description:
Whether the sign-in came from a mobile client. No mobile marker is stored with a connection, so the value
is `false` on every item and tells a caller nothing about the device.

ip.description:
The IP address the sign-in came from, with the port stripped off. On the item that matches `loginEvent` it
is taken from the address the current request arrives from instead of the one stored at sign-in.

country.description:
The English name of the country the IP address is located in. It is empty when the address cannot be
located, which is the normal outcome for private and loopback addresses.

city.description: The city the IP address is located in, empty under the same conditions as `country`.

browser.description:
The browser and its version as parsed from the user agent of the sign-in, empty when the client sent no
recognisable one. It is refreshed from the current request on the item that matches `loginEvent`.

platform.description:
The operating system as parsed from the user agent of the sign-in, refreshed and left empty under the same
conditions as `browser`.

date.description: When the sign-in happened, in the portal time zone rather than in UTC.

page.description:
Where in the portal the sign-in was made from: the referrer of the request that created it, or that
request's own path when it carried no referrer. Long values are cut off at 512 characters.

startDocsEnabled.description:

flags below it depends on nothing that has to be configured, so its built-in value is always `true`.

helpCenterEnabled.description:

userForumEnabled.description:

videoGuidesEnabled.description:

licenseAgreementsEnabled.description:

email.description:
The address the join link is sent to. It has to be a well-formed ASCII address rather than an
internationalized one, must not already belong to a member of the portal, and, where the portal trusts named
domains only, has to end with one of them; any of these faults is refused with 400.

culture.description:
The language the letter is written in, as a culture name such as `en-US`. A culture the installation does not
have falls back to the portal language rather than failing the call.

AdminMessageBaseSettingsRequestDto.description: Who is invited to join the portal, and in which language the invitation is written.

examples: Hello, this is a test message from the administrator.
message.description:
What the sender wants to tell the portal administrators. Markup is stripped before the letter is written, so
a body that carries nothing but markup counts as empty and is refused with 400.

email.description:
The address the sender can be answered at, which the letter is signed with. It has to be a well-formed email
address.

culture.description:
The language the letter is written in, as a culture name such as `en-US`. A culture the installation does not
have falls back to the portal language rather than failing the call.

recaptchaType.description:
Which CAPTCHA service the proof in `recaptchaResponse` came from. It has to match the service the
installation is configured with, which `GET api/2.0/capabilities` reports; the default value means the
installation is left to decide.

recaptchaResponse.description:
The token the CAPTCHA widget produced in the browser, passed on unchanged for the portal to verify with the
CAPTCHA service. It is single-use and short-lived, so it cannot be reused for a second message.

AdminMessageSettingsRequestDto.description: The message sent to the portal administrators, with the CAPTCHA proof that a person wrote it.

prompt.description:
The cost of one million tokens sent to the model, which includes the conversation history resent with
every turn and not just the newest message.

completion.description: The cost of one million tokens the model writes back. It is normally the dearer of the two directions.

promptCacheRead.description:
The cost of one million prompt tokens served from the prompt cache. It is absent when the model does not
support prompt caching.

promptCacheWrite.description:
The cost of one million prompt tokens written to the prompt cache with the default lifetime. It is absent
when the model does not support prompt caching.

promptCacheWrite1H.description:
The cost of one million prompt tokens written to the prompt cache with a one-hour lifetime. It is absent
when the model offers no such option.

AiChatPriceDto.description: What a chat model charges, split by the direction the tokens flow in.

prompt.description:
The cost of one million tokens turned into vectors. Embedding produces no completion, so this single
figure is the whole price.

AiEmbeddingPriceDto.description: What an embedding model charges, which has one direction only.

id.description:
The model identifier to send to the AI operations. It is the value to branch on, while `alias` is for display
only.

alias.description: The model name as the vendor writes it, meant to be shown to a person rather than matched on.

provider.description:
Who runs the model: the built-in provider, or the vendor the portal's own key belongs to when `byok` is
true. Two entries can share a provider, and one provider's models can be priced quite differently, so
the price always belongs to the entry and never to the provider.

image.description: The absolute URL of the provider's icon, for rendering next to the entry.

price.description:
What the entry costs, in the currency the answer names. Amounts per token are normalised per million
tokens, so they are not the price of a single call. When `byok` is true it is the vendor's own price, which
the portal pays to the vendor directly.

byok.description:
Whether this portal calls the model with its own provider key (BYOK) instead of the built-in one; when
true, `provider`, `price` and `link` describe the vendor of that key.

link.description:
The provider's own page for the model, for a person to read the model's terms; for a BYOK entry, the
vendor's pricing page. It is empty when the provider publishes none.

reached, so pick one from this list rather than typing it.

displayName.description:
The region name as Amazon writes it, in English regardless of the portal language, for showing in a
picker next to `systemName`.

partitionName.description:
The Amazon partition the region sits in - the ordinary commercial cloud, the Chinese one, or a government
one. Regions of different partitions are not reachable with the same credentials.

partitionDnsSuffix.description: The domain the partition's service host names end in, which differs from partition to partition.

partitionRegionRegex.description: The pattern every region code of this partition matches, for validating a code before sending it.
