completed.description:
Whether the job has finished. This is the field to poll; the first answer that reports it true also discards
the job, so read `error` out of that same answer rather than calling again.

id.description:
The identifier of the queued job. A portal only ever has one test job at a time, so it names the run rather
than selecting among several.

error.description:
Why the test failed. It stays empty while the job runs and also once the relay has accepted the message, so
an empty value on a finished job is what success looks like; an unreachable relay is reported here after a
30-second connection timeout rather than as a failed request.

status.description:
The step the job has reached, in words - `Connect to host` or `Send test message`, for instance. It is meant
to be shown to a person and is not a fixed set of values to branch on.

percents.description:
How far the job has got, as a percentage climbing to 100. Reaching 100 says the job ran to the end, not that
the message was accepted - that is what an empty `error` says.

host.description:
The host name or address of the mail server. On a cloud portal that has saved no relay of its own every
field of this object comes back empty, because the installation's own server is not disclosed - only
`isDefaultSettings` is set there.

port.description:
The port the mail server is reached on - conventionally 25 or 587 without encryption from the start, 465
with it. It is empty when no port was stored, in which case the portal falls back to its own default.

senderAddress.description: The address the letters are sent from, which appears in the From header and is what a reply goes to.

senderDisplayName.description: The name shown beside that address in a recipient's mailbox.

credentialsUserName.description: The account the portal signs in to the mail server as, meaningful only while `enableAuth` is `true`.

credentialsUserPassword.description:
Always empty here: the stored password is never returned, so a client that sends these settings back has
to supply it again rather than echoing what it read.

enableSSL.description: Whether the connection to the mail server is encrypted.

enableAuth.description:
Whether the portal signs in to the mail server at all. While it is `false` the credentials above are
ignored and the server is expected to accept mail unauthenticated.

useNtlm.description:
Always `false` here: the flag is accepted when settings are saved but is not stored, so it never comes
back set and says nothing about how the portal authenticates.

isDefaultSettings.description:
Whether the portal is still on the mail configuration of the installation rather than on a relay of its
own. `DELETE api/2.0/smtpsettings/smtp` puts it back to `true`, and while it is `true` on a cloud portal
the fields above are blank rather than showing the installation's server.

saml20HttpPost.description:
The SAML 2.0 HTTP POST binding, which carries the request in a self-submitting form. It is what the
built-in configuration uses and the one to pick when requests are signed, since it has no length limit.

saml20HttpRedirect.description:
The SAML 2.0 HTTP redirect binding, which carries the request in the query string and is therefore bound
by the length a URL may have.

SsoBindingTypeDto.description: The SAML bindings the SSO settings accept.

selfSigned.description: Specifies if a certificate is self-signed or not.

SsoCertificateDto.description: A certificate used to sign or encrypt SAML messages, with its validity period.

aes128.description: The AES-128-CBC encryption algorithm, which the built-in configuration uses.

aes256.description: The AES-256-CBC encryption algorithm, the strongest of the three.

triDec.description: The Triple DES CBC encryption algorithm, kept for identity providers that support nothing newer.

SsoEncryptAlgorithmTypeDto.description: The encryption algorithms the SSO settings accept.

SsoFieldMappingDto.description: Which SAML attributes fill the profile fields of a user who signs in through SSO.

verification.description:
The certificate verifies the signatures on what the provider sends, and nothing else - the counterpart of
the service provider's signing action.

decrypt.description: The certificate is used to decrypt what the provider sends, but verifies no signature.

verificationAndDecrypt.description: The certificate does both, which is what a single provider certificate has to be set to.

SsoIdpCertificateActionTypeDto.description: What the identity provider's certificate may be used for, as the `action` of an identity provider certificate.

verifyAuthResponsesSign.description: Specifies if the signatures of the SAML authentication responses sent to SP will be verified or not.

verifyLogoutRequestsSign.description: Specifies if the signatures of the SAML logout requests sent to SP will be verified or not.

verifyLogoutResponsesSign.description: Specifies if the signatures of the SAML logout responses sent to SP will be verified or not.

decryptAssertions.description: Specifies if the assertions will be decrypted or not.

SsoIdpCertificateAdvancedDto.description: How the portal checks and decrypts what the identity provider sends.

SsoIdpSettingsDto.description: The identity provider the portal trusts: its entity id, endpoints and bindings.

saml11Unspecified.description: The SAML 1.1 unspecified name ID format.

saml11EmailAddress.description: The SAML 1.1 email address name ID format.

saml20Entity.description: The SAML 2.0 entity name ID format.

saml20Transient.description:
The SAML 2.0 transient name ID format, whose identifier differs from one session to the next. It is what
the built-in configuration uses.

saml20Persistent.description: The SAML 2.0 persistent name ID format, whose identifier stays the same for one person across sessions.

saml20Encrypted.description: The SAML 2.0 encrypted name ID format.

saml20Unspecified.description: The SAML 2.0 unspecified name ID format.

saml11X509SubjectName.description: The SAML 1.1 X.509 subject name name ID format.

saml11WindowsDomainQualifiedName.description: The SAML 1.1 Windows domain qualified name name ID format.

saml20Kerberos.description: The SAML 2.0 Kerberos name ID format.

SsoNameIdFormatTypeDto.description: The SAML name ID formats the SSO settings accept.

ssoNameIdFormatType.description:
The values the `nameIdFormat` of the identity provider settings accepts. The built-in configuration uses
the SAML 2.0 transient format.

ssoBindingType.description:
The values the `ssoBinding` and `sloBinding` of the identity provider settings accept - how the portal
sends its sign-in and sign-out requests. The built-in configuration uses HTTP POST for both.

ssoSigningAlgorithmType.description:
The values the `signingAlgorithm` of the service provider certificate and the `verifyAlgorithm` of the
identity provider certificate accept. The built-in configuration uses RSA-SHA1 for both.

ssoEncryptAlgorithmType.description:
The values the `encryptAlgorithm` and `decryptAlgorithm` of the certificate settings accept. The built-in
configuration uses AES-128 everywhere.

ssoSpCertificateActionType.description:
The values the `action` of a service provider certificate accepts, which is what the portal's own key
pair may be used for.

ssoIdpCertificateActionType.description:
The values the `action` of an identity provider certificate accepts, which is what the provider's
certificate may be used for - the mirror image of the service provider actions.

serializeSettings.description:
The configuration object serialised to a JSON string, not a nested object. It is the complete configuration
rather than a patch - fields left out are stored empty - so start from `GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2` or
`GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/default` and send back a changed copy. The identity provider entity ID and
sign-in URL are required, the sign-in and sign-out URLs have to be absolute `http` or `https` addresses, and
the attribute mapping has to name the first name, last name and email fields; the values each SAML field
accepts are listed by `GET api/2.0/settings/ssov2/constants`. An empty string, or a string that carries no
configuration object, is refused with 400.

id.description:
The provider's key, which is what `PUT api/2.0/settings/storage` and its CDN and backup counterparts take
as the storage to switch to. The built-in local storage has no entry of its own: a listing in which
nothing is `current` means the data sits locally.

title.description: The provider name in the portal language, falling back to `id` when this build ships no wording for it.

items.description: One key of an authorization provider or a storage, with how the settings form shows it.

properties.description:
The settings the provider expects, each with its key, its localised label and the value the server
currently holds. For the entry marked `current` the values come from the portal's saved storage settings
and for the others from the installation configuration, so a setting nobody has configured comes back with
an empty value rather than being left out.

current.description: Whether the portal is using this provider right now. At most one entry of a listing has it set.

isSet.description:
Whether the provider's keys are already filled in on the server, so it could be switched to without
sending credentials. It says nothing about whether the credentials still work.

StorageDto.description: One third-party storage provider the portal data can be kept in, with the keys it expects.

notifyUsers.description:
Whether every user of every portal on the server is mailed before the encryption or decryption pass starts.
The pass runs either way; the flag only decides whether people are told that their portal is about to become
unavailable.

StorageEncryptionRequestDto.description: Whether the users are warned before the portals go down for the storage encryption pass.

module.description:
The storage provider to switch to, by the identifier the matching listing operation reports - `default` for
the built-in local storage. The provider has to be available on the server, which that listing reports as
`isSet`, otherwise the request is refused with 400; sending the module already in use changes nothing.

items.description:
One entry of a keyed collection, carried as an explicit pair of `key` and `value` fields instead of as a member
of a JSON object, so that the key is not restricted to a string and the entries keep the order they are sent in.

props.description:
The credentials the provider expects, as the name and value pairs it defines - a bucket, a region and an
access key for an Amazon S3 storage, for instance. Read the expected names from the entry of that provider in
the listing operation; they differ per provider, so there is no fixed set.

lastModified.description: When the settings were last stored.

openSource.description:
Whether the installation runs the open-source build, which has no paid plan at all. This flag and the two
below describe the build rather than the subscription, and all three are left empty for a caller without
the portal-settings right.

enterprise.description:
Whether the installation runs on an Enterprise licence file, which is what makes the licence operations
under `api/2.0/settings/license` usable.

developer.description:
Whether the installation runs on a Developer licence, an Enterprise licence meant for embedding rather
than for production use.

id.description:
The identifier of the subscription record itself, for quoting when a charge has to be traced. It is filled
in for a caller with the portal-settings right only, and nothing accepts it as an argument.

state.description:
How the subscription stands: on trial, paid, inside the grace period that follows the due date, or unpaid.
It is the one field every caller gets, whatever their role, so a client can warn about payment without
needing administrator rights.

dueDate.description:
When the current period ends, in the portal time zone. It is filled in for a room or DocSpace
administrator only, and set to the largest value a date can hold for a subscription that never ends.

delayDueDate.description:
When the grace period after `dueDate` runs out and the portal is cut off, in the portal time zone. Filled
in under the same conditions as `dueDate`, and equal to it when the plan grants no grace period.

licenseDate.description:
When the licence file behind the subscription was issued, in the portal time zone. It is meaningful on a
server installation and filled in for a caller with the portal-settings right only.

customerId.description:
The account in the billing system the subscription is charged to, empty for a portal that has never been
billed. Filled in for a caller with the portal-settings right only.

items.description: One quota the subscription is made of - the plan itself or an add-on - with its quantity and its own deadline.

quotas.description:
The quotas the subscription is made of - the plan itself and its add-ons - with the overdue ones listed
alongside the current ones, so an entry here is not proof that it is still being paid for; read each
entry's own `state` for that. Filled in for a caller with the portal-settings right only.

TariffDto.description: The subscription this portal runs on: its state, the end of the current period, and the quotas it is made of.

id.description:
The quota this entry stands for. `GET api/2.0/portal/payment/quotas` describes the quota behind the ID,
including what its `quantity` counts; a negative ID belongs to a built-in quota rather than a purchased
one.

quantity.description:
How much of the quota the portal holds, in whatever the quota itself is measured in - seats for a plan,
gigabytes for storage. It is `1` for a quota that is simply on or off.

wallet.description:
Whether the quota is paid for out of the portal wallet as it is consumed, rather than being part of the
subscription charged per period.

additional.description:
Whether this is an add-on bought on top of the plan rather than the plan itself. Exactly one entry of
`quotas` is the plan, and the rest are add-ons.

dueDate.description:
When this quota runs out, in the portal time zone. An add-on can end earlier or later than the
subscription; a quota with no deadline of its own reports the subscription's `dueDate` instead of an empty
value.

nextQuantity.description:
The quantity the next period is going to be charged for, when a change has been scheduled. It is empty
while `quantity` simply carries over.

nextQuota.description:
The quota this one is scheduled to be replaced by at the start of the next period, empty when no such
switch is planned. `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff/upcoming` already reports the charge for the replacement.

state.description:
Whether the quota is still running or its deadline has passed. It is empty for a quota that has no
deadline of its own, which means it lasts as long as the subscription does.

TariffQuotaDto.description: One quota the subscription is made of - the plan itself or an add-on - with its quantity and its own deadline.

[0 - Trial, 1 - Paid, 2 - Delay, 3 - Not paid]

still waiting for it to be opened in Telegram. The waiting state ends on its own when the link expires,
so it is worth polling rather than treating as final.

affiliateId.description:
The partner the portal was signed up through, empty for a portal that came in directly. It is bookkeeping
for the vendor and has no bearing on what the portal may do.

tenantAlias.description:
The portal's own name within the installation, which together with the installation's base domain forms
the address it is reached at. A caller without the portal-settings right gets `tenantId` alone, so an
empty value here is the sign that the rest of this object was withheld rather than unset.

calls.description:
Whether telephony is switched on for the portal. It is carried over from portal registration and stays
`false` on a DocSpace portal, where the feature does not exist.

campaign.description:
The marketing campaign the portal was signed up under, empty for a portal that came in outside one. Like
`affiliateId`, it is bookkeeping only.

creationDateTime.description: When the portal was created, in UTC rather than in the portal time zone.

hostedRegion.description:
The data-centre region written on the portal record itself, as opposed to `region`, which is looked up
from the hosting service. It is empty on a server installation.

tenantId.description:
The numeric identifier of the portal inside the installation. It is the one field every caller gets,
whatever their rights.

industry.description:
The line of business chosen when the portal was created. It only steers what the vendor suggests and
restricts nothing.

language.description:
The default language of the portal as a culture name, the same value `GET api/2.0/settings` reports as
`culture`. A member may have a language of their own, which this does not reflect.

lastModified.description:
When any field of this record last changed, in UTC. It does not move when portal settings outside this
record are changed.

mappedDomain.description: The custom domain the portal answers on in addition to its own address, empty when none has been set up.

name.description:
The portal title as shown to people, which is what `GET api/2.0/settings` returns as
`greetingSettings`. It is free text, unlike `tenantAlias`, and empty until someone sets it.

ownerId.description:
The portal owner, the one account that cannot be removed or demoted.
`PUT api/2.0/settings/owner` hands the role over.

paymentId.description:
The portal's identifier in the billing system, empty for a portal that has never been billed. The
subscription itself is read with `GET api/2.0/portal/tariff`.

spam.description:
Whether the owner agreed to receive the vendor's newsletter. Despite the name it does not mark the portal
as a spammer and affects nothing but marketing mail.

status.description:
The lifecycle state of the portal. Anything other than active means most operations are refused for the
moment, because the portal is being transferred, restored, encrypted or removed.

statusChangeDate.description:
When `status` last changed, in UTC. For a portal pending removal it is the moment the countdown to
deletion started.

timeZone.description:
The portal time zone, which is the zone the dates this API calls "portal time" are expressed in. It may be
stored as a Windows identifier here, while `GET api/2.0/settings` always reports the IANA form.

trustedDomains.description:
The mail domains a new member may register or be invited from without confirming the address. It is empty
whenever `trustedDomainsType` is not `Custom`.

trustedDomainsRaw.description:
The same domains as the single stored string they are kept in, separated by commas. Read
`trustedDomains` instead; this one exists because it is what the record holds.

trustedDomainsType.description:
How the mail domains are applied: no domain trusted, every domain trusted, or only the listed ones. Only
the last of the three makes `trustedDomains` meaningful.

version.description:
The identifier of the portal version the installation pins this portal to, which is an internal number
and not the product version string that `GET api/2.0/settings` reports as `version`.

versionChanged.description:
When `version` last changed, in UTC. It stays at its zero value on a portal whose version has never been
switched.

region.description:
The data-centre region the portal is actually served from, looked up from the hosting service. It is
empty on a server installation and also whenever the installation's portal cache is switched off, so an
empty value does not mean the portal has no region - `hostedRegion` is the value from the record itself.

method, and authenticator activation or re-verification for the application method. The whole body is empty
when the portal requires no second factor of the caller.

cookieName.description:

authenticator-application method; the SMS method returns `url` alone.

cookieValue.description:
The value of that cookie. The call already set it on the response, so it is repeated here only for a client
that does not keep cookies of its own; it is filled in under the same condition as `cookieName`, and a
later call to this operation replaces it.

type.description:
The second factor the portal demands. The two methods are mutually exclusive, so switching one on switches
the other off, and any value outside the defined set is read as switching TFA off rather than refused.

id.description:
The account the request concerns, by portal user ID. Naming the portal owner is refused unless it is the
caller's own account. Where an operation detaches an authenticator application, the empty GUID and the
caller's own ID both mean the caller.

trustedIps.description:
The list of IP addresses that bypass TFA verification. Each entry is a single address, an inclusive
"from-to" range or a CIDR block. This is the whole list that is to hold afterwards, so send the addresses
already trusted along with a new one; an entry that cannot be parsed fails the call with 400, and accounts
named as mandatory still have to pass the challenge even from a trusted address.

mandatoryUsers.description:
The accounts that must pass the challenge whatever their address, by portal user ID. This is the whole list
that is to hold afterwards - leaving it out clears it rather than keeping it - and naming the portal owner is
refused unless the caller is the owner.

mandatoryGroups.description:
The groups whose members must pass the challenge whatever their address, by group ID. This is the whole list
that is to hold afterwards - leaving it out clears it rather than keeping it.

TfaRequestDto.description: The portal two-factor policy: which method is in force, who must pass it, and from where it is waived.

id.description:
Which method this entry describes: `sms` for a code sent by text message, `app` for a code from an
authenticator application. It is the value `PUT api/2.0/settings/tfaapp` takes as its `type`, and no other
value ever appears here.

title.description:
The label for the method in the portal language, meant for a button or a radio option. It is not stable
enough to branch on - match `id` for that.

enabled.description:
Whether this method is the portal's current policy. At most one entry can have it set, and none has it
while the portal challenges nobody. It says nothing about the caller's own account, which may be exempt
through `trustedIps` or forced through `mandatoryUsers`.

available.description:
Whether the method could be switched on at all. For `sms` it is `false` until the installation has a
working SMS provider, so a method can be offered here and still be impossible to enable; for `app` it is
always `true`.

trustedIps.description:
The addresses that skip the challenge, each either a single address, a `from-to` pair or a CIDR range. It
is empty when no address is exempt, which means every account is challenged.

mandatoryUsers.description:
The accounts that are challenged even from a trusted address, by user ID. Empty means the exemption in
`trustedIps` holds for everyone.

mandatoryGroups.description:
The groups whose members are challenged even from a trusted address, by group ID, with the same reading of
an empty list as `mandatoryUsers`.

TfaSettingsDto.description: One two-factor authentication method the portal offers, with the portal-wide state of that method.

account.description:
The label the authenticator application will list the credential under, which is the caller's own email
address. It identifies the entry to a person, and no application checks it.

manualEntryKey.description:
The secret in the base32 form that is typed into an application by hand. It describes the very same
credential as `qrCodeSetupImageUrl`, and repeating the call hands back the same value for the account until
the credential is reset.

qrCodeSetupImageUrl.description:
The same secret as a scannable image, given as a `data:image/png;base64,` URL that can be rendered
directly - it is not a link to fetch.

The plugin's description from its manifest, in the language the manifest was written in. The translations
of it are in `descriptionLocale`.

author.description:
Who wrote the plugin, as its manifest states it - not the portal member who uploaded it, who is
`createBy`.

homePage.description: The plugin's own page, for a person to read more about it. It is empty when the manifest names none.

pluginName.description:
The global the plugin registers itself under in the browser once its script has run, which is how a
client reaches it. It is distinct from `name`, the identifier the portal uses.

scopes.description: Which parts of the interface the plugin hooks into, as one comma-separated string rather than a list.

image.description:
The plugin's icon exactly as its manifest declares it, which is normally a file name inside the plugin's
own package rather than an absolute address - resolve it against the directory `url` points into.

createBy.description:
The portal member who uploaded the plugin. For a plugin that ships with the installation it is an empty
profile, since no member put it there.

createOn.description: When the plugin was uploaded. It stays at its zero value for a plugin that ships with the installation.

enabled.description:
Whether the portal loads the plugin. It is the state this portal stored, so an installation-wide plugin
can be on for one portal and off for another.

system.description:
Whether the plugin ships with the installation rather than having been uploaded here. A system plugin
cannot be deleted through `DELETE api/2.0/settings/webplugins/{name}`, only switched off.

url.description:
The address of the plugin's script, which a client loads to run it. It ends in a `hash` query taken from
`version`, so the address changes whenever the plugin is updated and an old one may be cached.

cssUrl.description: The absolute address of the plugin's stylesheet, empty for a plugin that ships none.

settings.description:
The settings string the portal keeps for the plugin, stored and returned verbatim - only the plugin knows
its shape. It is empty until `PUT api/2.0/settings/webplugins/{name}` saves one.

nameLocale.description:
The plugin's name translated, keyed by culture name. A culture that is missing falls back to `name`, and
the whole map is empty for a plugin that ships no translations.

descriptionLocale.description:
The plugin's description translated, keyed the same way as `nameLocale` and falling back to
`description`.

runtime.description:
How the script at `url` is to be loaded - as an ES module or as a classic script. It is empty for a
plugin whose manifest does not say, which a client treats as a classic script.

enabled.description:
Whether the plugin runs in this portal. Switching it on adds the domains its manifest declares to the portal

state without a reload.

settings.description:
The configuration the plugin reads at run time, as a JSON document serialised into a string. Its shape is
defined by the plugin and not by the portal, which stores it encrypted for this portal alone. It replaces
whatever was stored rather than merging into it, so send `{}` when there is nothing to keep.

name.description:
The event name exactly as it appears in a delivered payload, so a receiver can match on it. The entry
named `*` is not an event but the catch-all.

id.description:
The bit that stands for this event in the `triggers` bitmask of a subscription. Add the bits of the wanted
events together; the catch-all entry has the value `0` and is used on its own rather than added to
anything.

available.description:
Whether the caller's own role may subscribe to this event - a plain member cannot subscribe to user, group
or room creation, where a room administrator can. An unavailable event is listed all the same, and sending
its bit to `POST api/2.0/settings/webhook` is refused as an invalid request.

WebhookTriggerDto.description: One event a webhook can listen to, with the bit that selects it and whether the caller may subscribe to it.

id.description:
The identifier of the subscription, which is what `PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook`,
`DELETE api/2.0/settings/webhook/{id}` and the `configId` filter of the delivery log address it by.

name.description: The label the subscription was given, free text with no meaning to the portal.

uri.description:
The address every delivery is posted to. The signing secret that lets the receiver verify a delivery is
never part of this answer, so it has to be kept from the moment the subscription was created.

enabled.description:
Whether the subscription is delivering. While it is `false` events are dropped rather than queued, so
nothing arrives late after it is switched back on.

ssl.description:
Whether the certificate of `uri` is verified before a delivery. While it is `false` a self-signed
certificate is accepted as well.

triggers.description:
The events the subscription covers, as the bits of `GET api/2.0/settings/webhook/triggers` added
together. `0` is the catch-all, not none: it covers every event the subscription creator's current role may
receive, which can be fewer than all the events of the portal.

targetId.description:
The single entity the subscription is narrowed to, empty for a subscription that covers the whole portal. It
is the GUID of a user or group for user and group events, and the Files API entry ID of a file, folder or room
otherwise, kept as an opaque value, so a numeric ID, a third-party ID or a GUID can appear.

createdBy.description:
The member who created the subscription, which is also who a non-administrator is limited to seeing. It is
empty for a subscription created by a portal background job.

createdOn.description: When the subscription was created, in the portal time zone.

modifiedBy.description: The member who last changed the subscription, empty while nobody has changed it since it was created.

modifiedOn.description: When it was last changed, in the portal time zone, and empty under the same condition as `modifiedBy`.

lastFailureOn.description:
When a delivery last failed, in the portal time zone. It is empty for a subscription that has never
failed, and it is not cleared by a later success - compare it with `lastSuccessOn` to see which came last.

lastFailureContent.description:
What the target answered on that failure, truncated, for diagnosing without opening the delivery log. It
is empty when the failure produced no body at all, a timeout for instance.

lastSuccessOn.description:
When a delivery last succeeded, in the portal time zone, empty for a subscription that has never
delivered. Both this and `lastFailureOn` being empty means nothing has been attempted yet.

id.description:
The identifier of this delivery record, which is what `PUT api/2.0/settings/webhook/{id}/retry` re-sends.
The automatic retries of the delivery update this same record, while a manual retry gets a record and an
identifier of its own.

eventId.description:
The identifier of the event the delivery is for, which the receiver sees as `event.id` and in the
`x-docspace-event-id` header. It is the `id` of the event's first delivery record, so it equals `id` there and
stays the same on every manual retry, which makes it the value to group the records of one event by.

retriedBy.description:
The member who asked for this delivery with a manual retry. It is empty on the first delivery of an event,
which the portal sends by itself.

configName.description:
The name of the subscription the delivery belongs to. It is the name as it stands now, so it follows a
later rename of the subscription rather than recording what it was called at the time.

trigger.description:
The event that caused the delivery, as a single bit rather than a mask - a delivery is always for one
event, even though a subscription covers several.

creationTime.description:
When this delivery record was queued, as a UTC instant ending in `Z`. For the first delivery that is when the
event happened; for a manual retry it is the
moment of the retry. Records come back newest first by this moment.

method.description: The HTTP method the delivery was sent with, which is `POST` for every webhook the portal sends.

route.description:
The address the delivery is sent to: the subscription's URL as it stands now. The journal does not keep the
address of each attempt, so after the subscription's URL changes, an older record names the new one too.

requestHeaders.description:
The headers the portal sent, serialised as one string, including the signature header a receiver verifies
the payload with.

requestPayload.description:
The body the portal sent, which is the event payload as JSON text. It is stored as it was sent, so it
still describes the entity as it looked at the time of the event.

responseHeaders.description:
The headers the target answered with on the latest attempt, serialised the same way as `requestHeaders`. It
is empty until an attempt is answered, and when the target was not reached.

responsePayload.description:
The body the target answered with on the latest attempt, truncated for storage. Empty under the same
conditions as `responseHeaders`, and also for a target that answers with no body at all. A record the portal
stopped without sending holds the portal's own note here instead - a text that starts with `Not sent:` and
gives the reason - which is not an answer of the target: on a record that never went out `status` is then `0`
and `responseHeaders` is empty, while on one stopped after failed attempts they still describe the last of them.

status.description:
The HTTP status code the target answered on the latest attempt. It is `0` while the first attempt is still
on its way and on one that never reached the target, so `0` is not a failure code - it is the absence of an
answer. While `nextAttemptOn` is set it is the status of the failed attempt that caused the retry.

delivery.description:
When the successful answer came back, as a UTC instant ending in `Z` like `creationTime`. It stays empty until an
attempt succeeds, and for good once the portal has given up retrying.

attempts.description:
How many times the portal has tried to deliver this record so far. A failed attempt is retried with
growing pauses - on the default schedule about 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2, 5 and 10 hours, though
an installation may configure its own - all of them under the same record and the same
`x-docspace-event-id` header, so a receiver can drop a delivery it has already processed. The one exception
is a portal moved to another region while retries are pending: the moved records get new IDs, so the attempts
made there carry a new `x-docspace-event-id`.

nextAttemptOn.description:
When the next attempt is due, as a UTC instant ending in `Z` like `creationTime`. While an attempt is being sent
right now it holds the moment that attempt's lease expires, a few minutes ahead, rather than a scheduled retry;
it changes again once the attempt ends. Empty means no attempt will follow: the record is delivered, its retries
ran out, a manual retry of the same event took over from it, or the portal stopped it - because the subscription
was disabled or removed or its address rejected, the subscription's creator may no longer receive the event,
the stored body cannot be read or is in the payload format of a previous version, the portal is removed, the
record waited longer than the retry schedule allows, the portal was restored from a backup taken before the
record was answered, or the portal was moved to another region while the record was being sent. A stopped
record that was never attempted says why in `responsePayload`; one that was keeps the target's last answer there.

WebhooksLogDto.description:
One delivery of a webhook event, updated in place by its automatic retries: what was sent where, and what came
back the last time. A manual retry is a delivery record of its own for the same event.

type.description:
Which branding slot this entry describes. `Notification` is part of the type but never appears here: that
logo is derived from the login-page one and used only in letters.

name.description:
The stable name of the same slot, which is what `GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos/isdefault` keys its
entries by. It is a name to match on, not a file name.

size.description:
The pixel box the slot is drawn in. Only `width` and `height` carry information here; the resize flags and
offsets alongside them are left at their defaults and say nothing about how an uploaded image is treated.

path.description: The absolute URLs to render the slot from, one per theme.

WhiteLabelItemDto.description: One branding logo slot of the portal: the size it is drawn at, and where its images are served from.

light.description:
The absolute URL of the image to render on a light background. It is filled in unless the request asked
for the dark theme alone with `isDark=true`, in which case only `dark` comes back.

dark.description:
The absolute URL of the image to render on a dark background. When both themes are asked for it comes back
empty for a slot that has no separate dark image, meaning the light one is to be used for both; when
`isDark=false` was passed it is left out entirely.

WhiteLabelItemPathDto.description: The image URLs of one logo slot, per interface theme.

aspectRatio.description:
Whether the numbers are to be read as an aspect ratio rather than as pixels. Always `false` on the sizes
this API reports.

fillArea.description: Whether an image would be scaled to cover the box rather than to fit inside it. Always `false` here.

greater.description: Whether scaling would apply only to an image larger than the box. Always `false` here.

height.description: The height of the box in pixels - one of the two fields of this object that carry information.

ignoreAspectRatio.description: Whether scaling would be allowed to distort the image. Always `false` here.

isPercentage.description: Whether `width` and `height` are to be read as percentages. Always `false` here, so both are pixels.

less.description: Whether scaling would apply only to an image smaller than the box. Always `false` here.

limitPixels.description:
Whether the box is to be read as a total pixel-area budget instead of as two dimensions. Always `false`
here.

width.description: The width of the box in pixels - the other field of this object that carries information.

x.description: The horizontal offset of the box from the origin. Always `0` here.

y.description: The vertical offset of the box from the origin. Always `0` here.

WhiteLabelItemSizeDto.description: The pixel box a logo slot is drawn in, in the shape the imaging library reports a geometry.

oneOf.description: [LightSmall - Light small, LoginPage - Login page, Favicon - Favicon, DocsEditor - Docs editor, DocsEditorEmbed - Docs editor embed, LeftMenu - Left menu, AboutPage - About page, Notification - Notification, SpreadsheetEditor - Spreadsheet editor, SpreadsheetEditorEmbed - Spreadsheet editor embed, PresentationEditor - Presentation editor, PresentationEditorEmbed - Presentation editor embed, PdfEditor - Pdf editor, PdfEditorEmbed - Pdf editor embed, DiagramEditor - Diagram editor, DiagramEditorEmbed - Diagram editor embed]

[1 - Light small, 2 - Login page, 3 - Favicon, 4 - Docs editor, 5 - Docs editor embed, 6 - Left menu, 7 - About page, 8 - Notification, 9 - Spreadsheet editor, 10 - Spreadsheet editor embed, 11 - Presentation editor, 12 - Presentation editor embed, 13 - Pdf editor, 14 - Pdf editor embed, 15 - Diagram editor, 16 - Diagram editor embed]

WhiteLabelLogoType.description: The place a white-label logo is shown in.

logoText.description:
The wordmark printed next to or instead of a logo image, on the login page, in the editors and in
notification letters. An empty or blank value, and the built-in `ONLYOFFICE` itself, clear the setting rather
than store it. The text is not rendered into the logo images, which carry their own wordmark.

items.description:
One entry of a keyed collection, carried as an explicit pair of `key` and `value` fields instead of as a member
of a JSON object, so that the key is not restricted to a string and the entries keep the order they are sent in.

logo.description:
The logo images to store, each entry naming a logo slot in its `key` - the numeric `type` published by
`GET api/2.0/settings/whitelabel/logos` - and carrying the two theme images in its value. A slot left out of
the list keeps the image it has, so this is a partial update rather than a replacement of the whole branding.
Saving the login-page slot also rebuilds the notification logo from it.

WhiteLabelRequestDto.description: The branding a portal is given: the wordmark, the logo images, or both.

email.description:
The address the portal owner account is created with, which is also the address every administrative letter
goes to afterwards. It has to be a well-formed email address; a malformed one leaves the wizard unfinished.

passwordHash.description:
The owner password, already hashed in the client rather than sent in the clear. Hash it with the `salt`,
iteration count and hash size that `GET api/2.0/settings?withpassword=true` publishes, so the portal can
recognise it later; an empty value leaves the wizard unfinished.

lng.description:
The portal interface language, as a culture name such as `en-US`. It has to be one of the cultures enabled
for the installation, and an unknown one leaves the shipped default in place instead of failing the wizard.

timeZone.description:
The time zone every portal date is rendered in, as an IANA identifier such as `Europe/Riga`. A value that
matches nothing falls back to UTC rather than failing the wizard.

amiId.description:
The identifier of the Amazon Machine Image the portal was launched from, for an installation started from an
AWS image. It is recorded for the installation record only and changes nothing about the portal; leave it out
anywhere else.

subscribeFromSite.description:
Whether the owner agrees to receive product news at the address in `email`. It is a mailing consent and has
no bearing on the portal notifications, which are subscribed separately.

WizardRequestDto.description: What the initial setup wizard needs to finish a new portal: the owner credentials and the portal locale.

completed.description: Specifies if the Wizard settings are completed or not

lastModified.description: The timestamp indicating when the settings were last modified.

WizardSettingsDto.description: The state of the portal's first-run setup wizard.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Sliding window rate limit: 1500 requests per minute per user/IP.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Number of requests remaining in the current sliding window (1500 req/min). Concurrent limits also apply: 50 parallel GET requests, 15 parallel POST/PUT requests.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the current sliding window rate limit resets.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Up to 60s for the sliding window (1500 req/min), up to 86400s for the daily POST/PUT limit (10000/day).

Bearer.description: Enter 'Bearer {JWT Token}'. Tokens are validated per RFC8725 (JSON Web Token Best Current Practices): signatures are required and checked against a server-side algorithm allow-list (ES256, RS256) rather than the token header, and issuer, audience and expiry are all verified.

ApiKeyBearer.description: Authentication is determined by the 'Authorization' header
ApiKeyBearer.name: ApiKeyBearer

OAuth2.description: OAuth2 flow with Authorization Code. The access tokens it issues are JWTs, validated per RFC8725 exactly as the Bearer scheme describes.
